title.zh: 卷一百七十六 列傳第一百零一 韓愈附:孟郊 張籍 賈島
title.en: Volume 176 Biographies 101: Han Yu and Relatives, Meng Jiao, Zhang Ji, Jia Dao
title.raw: 卷一百七十六 列傳第一百零一 韓愈附:孟郊 張籍 賈島 Volume 176 Biographies 101: Han Yu and Relatives, Meng Jiao, Zhang Ji, Jia Dao

sentences.zh: 韓愈附:孟郊 張籍 皇甫湜 盧仝 賈島 劉乂

translations.literal: Han Yu, with appended [biographies]: Meng Jiao, Zhang Ji, Huangfu Shi, Lu Tong, Jia Dao, Liu Yi
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu, with appended biographies: Meng Jiao, Zhang Ji, Huangfu Shi, Lu Tong, Jia Dao, and Liu Yi

sentences.zh: 韓愈，字退之，鄧州南陽人。

translations.literal: Han Yu, style name Tuizhi, was a man of Nanyang in Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu, whose style name was Tuizhi, came from Nanyang in Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 七世祖茂，有功于後魏，封安定王。

translations.literal: His seventh-generation ancestor Mao had merit toward the Later Wei and was enfeoffed as Prince of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: His seventh-generation ancestor Mao had served the Northern Wei with distinction and was enfeoffed as Prince of Anding.

sentences.zh: 父仲卿，為武昌令，有美政，既去，縣人刻石頌德。

translations.literal: His father Zhongqing served as magistrate of Wuchang; he had excellent governance, and after he left, the county people carved stone to praise his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongqing had been magistrate of Wuchang and governed well; when he left office, the people of the county erected a stone inscription in praise of his virtue.

sentences.zh: 終秘書郎。

translations.literal: He ended as Secretary of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as a secretary in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 愈生三歲而孤，隨伯兄會貶官嶺表。

translations.literal: Yu was orphaned at three years; he followed his elder brother Hui, who was demoted to an office beyond the Lingnan passes.
translations.idiomatic: Yu lost his father when he was three and went with his elder brother Hui, who had been demoted to a post in the far south beyond the Lingnan passes.

sentences.zh: 會卒，嫂鄭鞠之。

translations.literal: When Hui died, his sister-in-law Lady Zheng raised him.
translations.idiomatic: After Hui died, his sister-in-law Lady Zheng brought Yu up.

sentences.zh: 愈自知讀書，日記數千百言，比長，盡能通《六經》、百家學。

translations.literal: From the time Yu knew how to read, he memorized several thousand words daily; when he grew up, he could thoroughly master the Six Classics and the learning of the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: Once he could read, Yu memorized several thousand characters a day, and by adulthood he had mastered the Six Classics and the teachings of the hundred schools.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第。

translations.literal: He was selected in the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi civil examination.

sentences.zh: 會董晉為宣武節度使，表署觀察推官。

translations.literal: When Dong Jin became military commissioner of Xuanwu, he memorialized and appointed [Yu] as investigating and pushing official.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Jin became military commissioner of Xuanwu, he recommended Yu for appointment as investigating commissioner.

sentences.zh: 晉卒，愈從喪出，不四日，汴軍亂，乃去。

translations.literal: When Jin died, Yu followed the funeral procession out; within four days the Bian army rebelled, and he then left.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin died, Yu accompanied the funeral cortege out of the city; within four days the Bianzhou garrison mutinied, and he departed.

sentences.zh: 依武甯節度使張建封，建封辟府推官。

translations.literal: He relied on Zhang Jianfeng, military commissioner of Wuning; Jianfeng recruited him as headquarters pushing official.
translations.idiomatic: He attached himself to Zhang Jianfeng, military commissioner of Wuning, who took him on as a staff pushing official.

sentences.zh: 操行堅正，鯁言無所忌。

translations.literal: His conduct was firm and upright; he spoke bluntly without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct was upright and resolute, and he spoke his mind bluntly without fear.

sentences.zh: 調四門博士，遷監察御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Four Gates erudite, then promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to erudite of the Four Gates Academy and then promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 上疏極論宮市，德宗怒，貶陽山令。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial vehemently criticizing the palace market; Emperor Dezong was angry and demoted him to magistrate of Yangshan.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne with a forceful critique of the palace market; Emperor Dezong was enraged and demoted him to magistrate of Yangshan.

sentences.zh: 有愛在民，民生子多以其姓字之。

translations.literal: He had affection toward the people; when the people bore sons, many used his surname to name them.
translations.idiomatic: The people loved him, and when they had sons many named them with his surname.

sentences.zh: 改江陵法曹參軍。

translations.literal: He was changed to legal bureau aide of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as legal bureau aide in Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 元和初，權知國子博士，分司東都，三歲為真。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhe reign, he was acting director of studies of the National University, with a branch post at the Eastern Capital; after three years he received the regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanhe era he served as acting erudite of the Imperial University on detached duty at the Eastern Capital, and after three years received a regular appointment.

sentences.zh: 改都官員外郎，即拜河南令。

translations.literal: He was changed to vice director of the Capital Office, then immediately appointed magistrate of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the Capital Office and then immediately appointed magistrate of Henan.

sentences.zh: 遷職方員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 華陰令柳澗有罪，前刺史劾奏之，未報而刺史罷。

translations.literal: Liu Jian, magistrate of Huayin, had guilt; the former prefect impeached and memorialized him, but before a reply the prefect was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian, magistrate of Huayin, had committed offenses; the previous prefect had impeached him, but before a response arrived that prefect had left office.

sentences.zh: 澗諷百姓遮索軍頓役直，後刺史惡之，按其獄，貶澗房州司馬。

translations.literal: Jian incited the common people to block and demand army camp labor fees; the later prefect hated this, investigated his case, and demoted Jian to army vice-commandant of Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had urged the people to intercept troops and demand payment for billeting and corvée; the new prefect took offense, investigated the case, and demoted Jian to army vice-commandant in Fang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 愈過華，以為刺史陰相党，上疏治之。

translations.literal: When Yu passed through Hua, he believed the prefect was secretly protecting a faction and submitted a memorial to prosecute him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu passed through Huayin, he believed the prefect was secretly shielding Jian and memorialized the throne to have him punished.

sentences.zh: 既御史覆問，得澗贓，再貶封溪尉。

translations.literal: After the censorate reinvestigated, Jian's corruption was established, and [Yu] was demoted again to commandant of Fengxi.
translations.idiomatic: When the censorate reinvestigated, Jian's guilt was confirmed, and Yu was demoted again to commandant of Fengxi.

sentences.zh: 愈坐是復為博士。

translations.literal: Because of this Yu again became an erudite.
translations.idiomatic: On account of this affair Yu was again made an erudite.

sentences.zh: 既才高數黜，官又下遷，乃作《進學解》以自諭曰：

translations.literal: Since his talent was high yet he was repeatedly dismissed and his office again demoted, he composed "Discourse on Advancing in Learning" to instruct himself, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Having been dismissed again despite his great talent and demoted once more in rank, he wrote "Discourse on Advancing in Learning" to explain himself, which reads:

sentences.zh: 國子先生晨入太學，召諸生立館下，誨之曰：「業精於勤，荒於嬉；

translations.literal: The Academician of the National University at dawn entered the Imperial Academy, summoned the students to stand below the hall, and instructed them, saying: "Mastery of one's craft comes from diligence and is ruined by play;
translations.idiomatic: The director of the Imperial University entered the academy at dawn, called the students to assemble below the lecture hall, and admonished them: "Excellence in study comes from diligence and is lost to idleness;

sentences.zh: 行成于思，毀於隨。

translations.literal: conduct is completed through thought and destroyed through laxity.
translations.idiomatic: conduct is formed through reflection and undone through carelessness.

sentences.zh: 方今聖賢相逢，治具畢張，拔去凶邪，登崇畯良。

translations.literal: Now sage and worthy meet; instruments of governance are fully deployed; the vicious and depraved are uprooted, and the worthy and good are elevated.
translations.idiomatic: In this age sage and worthy men stand together, the tools of good government are fully in place, the wicked are rooted out, and the capable are raised up.

sentences.zh: 占小善者率以錄，名一藝者無不庸。

translations.literal: Those who possess small virtues are generally enrolled; those famed for a single skill are all employed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who show even modest merit are generally enrolled, and anyone renowned for a single art finds employment.

sentences.zh: 爬羅剔抉，刮垢磨光。

translations.literal: They comb, sift, pick, and choose; they scrape away filth and polish to a shine.
translations.idiomatic: Talents are gathered, sifted, and chosen; roughness is scraped away and brilliance brought forth.

sentences.zh: 蓋有幸而獲選，孰雲多而不揚？

translations.literal: If by chance one is selected, who would say that because there are many, none are promoted?
translations.idiomatic: If you are fortunate enough to be chosen, who can say that talent is too abundant for anyone to rise?

sentences.zh: 諸生業患不能精，無患有司之不明；

translations.literal: Students, worry that your studies cannot be refined—do not worry that the authorities are not perceptive;
translations.idiomatic: Students, your concern should be that your studies are not thorough, not that the examiners lack discernment;

sentences.zh: 行患不能成，無患有司之不公。」

translations.literal: worry that your conduct cannot be completed—do not worry that the authorities are not fair."
translations.idiomatic: worry that your conduct is not formed, not that the examiners are unjust."

sentences.zh: 言未既，有笑於列者曰：「先生欺予哉！

translations.literal: Before the words were finished, someone in the ranks laughed and said: "Sir, you deceive me!
translations.idiomatic: He had not finished speaking when someone in the assembly laughed and said, "Sir, you are deceiving us!

sentences.zh: 弟子事先生，于茲有年矣。

translations.literal: Your disciple has served you, sir, for years now.
translations.idiomatic: I have studied under you for years now.

sentences.zh: 先生口不絕吟於六藝之文，手不停披於百家之編。

translations.literal: Sir, your mouth never ceases chanting the texts of the Six Arts; your hand never stops turning the pages of the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: You never stop reciting the texts of the Six Classics, and your hand never rests from turning the pages of the hundred schools.

sentences.zh: 記事者必提其要，纂言者必鉤其玄。

translations.literal: When recording events you always seize the essentials; when compiling words you always hook the profound.
translations.idiomatic: When reading histories you always grasp the essentials; when studying treatises you always probe their deepest meaning.

sentences.zh: 貪多務得，細大不捐。

translations.literal: Greedy for much and striving to obtain, you reject neither small nor great.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy for learning and striving to master it all, you spare neither the minute nor the vast.

sentences.zh: 燒膏油以繼晷，常矻矻以窮年。

translations.literal: You burn lamp oil to extend the daylight and constantly toil through the year.
translations.idiomatic: You burn lamp oil to lengthen the day and labor tirelessly year after year.

sentences.zh: 先生之業，可謂勤矣。

translations.literal: Sir, in your studies you may be called diligent.
translations.idiomatic: In scholarship, sir, you may truly be called diligent.

sentences.zh: 牴排異端，攘斥佛老。

translations.literal: You resist and expel heterodox teachings and drive away Buddhism and Daoism.
translations.idiomatic: You oppose heterodox doctrines and repudiate Buddhism and Daoism.

sentences.zh: 補苴罅漏，張惶幽眇。

translations.literal: You patch gaps and leaks and extend what is obscure and subtle.
translations.idiomatic: You mend what is torn in the tradition and bring forth what is hidden and subtle.

sentences.zh: 尋墜緒之芒芒，獨旁搜而遠紹。

translations.literal: You seek the fallen thread in its vast obscurity, alone searching widely and transmitting from afar.
translations.idiomatic: You seek out the lost thread of the tradition in its vast obscurity, searching widely on your own and carrying it forward from distant antiquity.

sentences.zh: 停百川而東之，回狂瀾於既倒。

translations.literal: You dam the hundred streams and turn them eastward; you turn back the raging billows already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: You gather the hundred streams and turn them eastward; you turn back the raging tide already run to ruin.

sentences.zh: 先生之于儒，可謂有勞矣。

translations.literal: Sir, in regard to Confucianism, you may be said to have labored.
translations.idiomatic: In service to Confucian learning, sir, you have truly labored.

sentences.zh: 沈浸濃郁，含英咀華。

translations.literal: You steep yourself in richness and density; you hold the flower and chew the blossom.
translations.idiomatic: You steep yourself in the rich fragrance of literature and savor its finest blossoms.

sentences.zh: 作為文章，其書滿家。

translations.literal: In composing literary works, your writings fill the house.
translations.idiomatic: As a writer of literature, your works fill the house.

sentences.zh: 上規姚姒，渾渾亡涯。

translations.literal: Above you take Yao and Si as models; vast and boundless without limit.
translations.idiomatic: You take Yao and Si as your models above; your style is vast and without limit.

sentences.zh: 周《誥》商《盤》，佶屈聱牙。

translations.literal: The Zhou "Announcements" and Shang "Pan" are stiff, twisted, and hard to pronounce.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou "Announcements" and Shang "Pan" are stiff and hard on the tongue.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》謹嚴，《左氏》浮誇。

translations.literal: The "Spring and Autumn" is strict and severe; the "Zuo Tradition" is floating and exaggerated.
translations.idiomatic: The "Spring and Autumn" is austere and exacting; the "Zuo Tradition" is florid and expansive.

sentences.zh: 《易》奇而法，《詩》正而葩。

translations.literal: The "Changes" is strange yet patterned; the "Odes" is upright yet ornate.
translations.idiomatic: The "Changes" is marvelous yet methodical; the "Odes" is upright yet richly adorned.

sentences.zh: 下迨《莊》《騷》，太史所錄，子雲相如，同工異曲。

translations.literal: Below reaching "Zhuangzi" and "Li Sao," what the Grand Historian recorded, Ziyun and Xiangru—same craft, different tunes.
translations.idiomatic: Below you reach "Zhuangzi" and "Li Sao," the records of the Grand Historian, Yang Xiong and Sima Xiangru—same mastery, different styles.

sentences.zh: 先生之于文，可謂閎其中而肆其外矣。

translations.literal: Sir, in literature you may be said to be vast within and expansive without.
translations.idiomatic: In literature, sir, you are vast within and magnificent without.

sentences.zh: 少始知學，勇於敢為。

translations.literal: In youth you first knew learning and were bold in daring action.
translations.idiomatic: In youth you first took up learning and were bold in what you dared to do.

sentences.zh: 長通于方，左右具宜。

translations.literal: Grown up, you mastered methods; in every direction all is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: As you matured you mastered every method and are adept in all directions.

sentences.zh: 先生之于為人，可謂成矣。

translations.literal: Sir, as a person you may be called complete.
translations.idiomatic: As a man, sir, you may be called fully formed.

sentences.zh: 然而公不見信於人，私不見助于友。

translations.literal: Yet publicly you are not trusted by others; privately you receive no help from friends.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in public you win no trust, and in private your friends give you no aid.

sentences.zh: 跋前躓後，動輒得咎。

translations.literal: Stumbling forward and tripping back, at every move you incur blame.
translations.idiomatic: You trip going forward and stumble going back; at every turn you invite censure.

sentences.zh: 暫為御史，遂竄南夷。

translations.literal: Briefly a censor, then banished to the southern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: You were briefly a censor, then driven off to the southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 三年博士，冗不見治。

translations.literal: Three years as erudite, superfluous and not seen as effective in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Three years as erudite, a post so idle that no one considers you fit for real administration.

sentences.zh: 命與仇謀，取敗幾時？

translations.literal: Fate plots with enmity—how long before defeat is taken?
translations.idiomatic: Fate conspires with your enemies—how long before you are utterly ruined?

sentences.zh: 冬暖而兒號寒，年豐而妻啼饑。

translations.literal: Winter is warm yet your sons cry of cold; the year is abundant yet your wife weeps of hunger.
translations.idiomatic: The winter is mild yet your sons cry of cold; the harvest is good yet your wife weeps of hunger.

sentences.zh: 頭童齒豁，竟死何裨？

translations.literal: Head bald and teeth fallen out—what use if you die at the end?
translations.idiomatic: Your head is bald and your teeth are gone—what good will it do you to die at last?

sentences.zh: 不知慮此，而反教人為？」

translations.literal: You do not know to consider this, yet instead teach others how to act?"
translations.idiomatic: You never think of this yourself, yet you presume to teach others how to live?"

sentences.zh: 先生曰：「吁！

translations.literal: The Academician said: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: The director said, "Alas!

sentences.zh: 子來前。

translations.literal: Come forward.
translations.idiomatic: Come here.

sentences.zh: 夫大木為杗，細木為桷，欂櫨侏儒，椳闑磺楔，各得其所，施以成室者，匠氏之工也。

translations.literal: Large timber becomes ridgepoles, small timber becomes rafters; bracket arms, dwarf pillars, door panels, door bolts, door pivots, and wedges—each finds its place, and when applied a room is completed: this is the carpenter's craft.
translations.idiomatic: Great timbers serve as ridgepoles and small timbers as rafters; bracket arms, dwarf posts, door panels, pivots, and wedges—each is put where it belongs so that a house may be built: that is the carpenter's art.

sentences.zh: 玉劄丹砂，赤箭青芝，牛溲馬勃，敗鼓之皮，俱收並蓄，待用無遺者，醫師之良也。

translations.literal: Jade hairpins, cinnabar, red arrowroot, blue fungus, cow dung, horse lichen, the skin of a broken drum—all are gathered and stored, kept for use without omission: this is the good physician's way.
translations.idiomatic: Jade hairpins, cinnabar, red arrowroot, blue lingzhi, cow dung, horse lichen, the skin of a ruined drum—all are gathered and kept ready for use without waste: that is the mark of a skilled physician.

sentences.zh: 登明選公，雜進巧拙，紆餘為妍，卓犖為傑，校短量長，唯器是適者，宰相之方也。

translations.literal: Promoting the bright and selecting the capable, mixing the skilled and the clumsy, turning what is circuitous into beauty and what is outstanding into excellence, comparing short and measuring long, fitting only to capacity—this is the prime minister's method.
translations.idiomatic: Elevating the capable and choosing the fit, mixing the adept with the awkward, finding grace in what is indirect and excellence in what stands out, weighing strengths against weaknesses and assigning each to his proper role—that is how a chief minister governs.

sentences.zh: 昔者孟軻好辯，孔道以明；

translations.literal: Formerly Mencius loved disputation, and the way of Confucius was thereby clarified;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Mencius loved debate, and through him the way of Confucius was made clear;

sentences.zh: 轍環天下，卒老於行。

translations.literal: his carriage tracks circled the realm, and in the end he aged upon the road.
translations.idiomatic: his carriage wheels circled the empire, yet in the end he grew old upon the road.

sentences.zh: 荀卿宗王，大倫以興；

translations.literal: Xun Qing honored kings, and the great norms were thereby raised;
translations.idiomatic: Xunzi exalted kingship, and the great moral order was thereby revived;

sentences.zh: 逃讒于楚，廢死蘭陵。

translations.literal: he fled slander in Chu and died in disuse at Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: he fled slander to Chu and died in obscurity at Lanling.

sentences.zh: 是二儒者，吐詞為經，舉足為法，絕類離倫，優入聖域，其遇於世何如也？

translations.literal: These two Confucians—when they spoke, their words were canon; when they stepped, their steps were law; they surpassed their kind and left their peers; they entered the sage's domain with excellence—what was their encounter with the world like?
translations.idiomatic: These two Confucians—whose words were scripture and whose steps were law, who surpassed their kind and stood apart from their peers, who nearly entered the domain of the sages—what was their lot in the world?

sentences.zh: 今先生學雖勤而不由其統，言雖多而不要其中；

translations.literal: Now, sir, though your learning is diligent, you do not follow its orthodox lineage; though your words are many, you do not grasp their center;
translations.idiomatic: Now, sir, for all your diligence in study you do not follow the orthodox tradition; for all your many words you miss their essential point;

sentences.zh: 文雖奇而不濟於用，行雖修而不顯於眾。

translations.literal: though your literature is strange, it does not aid in practical use; though your conduct is cultivated, it does not shine before the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: for all the strangeness of your writing it serves no practical end; for all the cultivation of your conduct you win no renown among the people.

sentences.zh: 猶且月費俸錢，歲靡稟粟，子不知耕，婦不知織；

translations.literal: yet month by month you spend salary money, year by year you consume allotted grain; your sons do not know how to plow, your wife does not know how to weave;
translations.idiomatic: Yet month after month you draw your salary, year after year you consume your grain allotment; your sons cannot plow, your wife cannot weave;

sentences.zh: 乘馬從徒，安坐而食；

translations.literal: you ride horses followed by attendants and sit at ease while eating.
translations.idiomatic: you ride with attendants in train and eat your fill while sitting idle.

sentences.zh: 踵常途之促促，窺陳編以盜竊。

translations.literal: You tread the cramped common path and peep at old compilations to pilfer.
translations.idiomatic: You plod the cramped beaten path and rifle old texts for scraps to steal.

sentences.zh: 然而聖主不加誅，宰臣不見斥。

translations.literal: Yet the sage ruler does not punish you, and the chief minister does not dismiss you.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the sage ruler does not punish you, and the chief minister does not cast you out.

sentences.zh: 茲非其幸歟？

translations.literal: Is this not your good fortune?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not your good fortune?

sentences.zh: 動而得謗，名亦隨之。

translations.literal: When you move you incur slander, and your fame follows with it.
translations.idiomatic: When you stir you draw slander, and fame follows in its wake.

sentences.zh: 投閒置散，乃分之宜。

translations.literal: Cast into leisure and set aside in idleness—this is what your allotment properly warrants.
translations.idiomatic: To be cast into an idle post and set aside—that is what your lot properly warrants.

sentences.zh: 若夫商財賄之有無，計班資之崇庳，忘量己之所稱，指前人之瑕疵，是所謂詰匠氏之不以杙為楹，而訾醫師以昌陽引年，欲進其豨苓也。」

translations.literal: As for bargaining over whether wealth and bribes exist, calculating whether ranks and salaries are high or low, forgetting to measure what suits yourself, and pointing out the flaws of predecessors—this is what is called interrogating the carpenter for not using a peg as a pillar, and blaming the physician for using cypress to prolong life while wanting to advance one's own poria cocos."
translations.idiomatic: As for haggling over wealth and bribes, reckoning whether rank and salary are high or low, forgetting to measure your own worth, and picking at the faults of your betters—that is like berating the carpenter for not making a peg into a pillar, or blaming the physician for prescribing cypress to prolong life while demanding he give you poria instead."

sentences.zh: 執政覽之，奇其才，改比部郎中、史館修撰。

translations.literal: Those in power read it, marveled at his talent, and changed him to director of the Revenue Bureau and compiler at the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers read it, admired his talent, and transferred him to director of the Revenue Bureau and compiler at the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 轉考功，知制誥，進中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Bureau of Merit, made drafter of edicts, and advanced to Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Bureau of Merit, appointed drafter of edicts, and promoted to drafter of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，憲宗將平蔡，命御史中丞裴度使諸軍按視。

translations.literal: Initially, when Emperor Xianzong was about to pacify Cai, he ordered Vice Censor-in-Chief Pei Du to go to the armies to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Xianzong was preparing to pacify Cai Prefecture, he ordered Vice Censor-in-Chief Pei Du to inspect the various armies.

sentences.zh: 及還，且言賊可滅，與宰相議不合。

translations.literal: When he returned, he also said the rebels could be destroyed, but his discussion with the chief ministers did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he reported that the rebels could be destroyed, but his views did not align with those of the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 愈亦奏言：

translations.literal: Yu also memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yu also submitted a memorial, which read:

sentences.zh: 淮西連年脩器械防守，金帛糧畜耗於給賞，執兵之卒四向侵掠，農夫織婦餉於其後，得不償費。

translations.literal: In Huai West for successive years they repaired weapons and defended; gold, silk, grain, and livestock were consumed in bestowing rewards; soldiers bearing arms raided in the four directions; farmers and weaving women supplied them from behind—the gain did not repay the cost.
translations.idiomatic: For years Huai West had been repairing arms and holding defensive lines; gold, silk, grain, and livestock were drained away in rewards; armed troops raided on every side while farmers and weaving women supplied them from behind—the cost far outweighed any gain.

sentences.zh: 比聞畜馬皆上槽櫪，此譬有十夫之力，自朝抵夕，跳躍叫呼，勢不支久，必自委頓。

translations.literal: Recently it was heard that the horses kept were all put in mangers and stalls; this is like having the strength of ten men who from morning until evening leap and shout—the force cannot endure long and must collapse of itself.
translations.idiomatic: I have lately heard that their horses are all stabled and fed in stalls; this is like ten strong men leaping and shouting from dawn till dusk—the strain cannot last, and they are bound to collapse on their own.

sentences.zh: 當其已衰，三尺童子可制其命。

translations.literal: When they have already declined, a three-foot child can control their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Once they have weakened, even a small child can take their lives.

sentences.zh: 況以三州殘弊困劇之餘而當天下全力，其敗可立而待也，然未可知者，在陛下斷與不斷耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, with the three prefectures in the aftermath of ruin, exhaustion, and extreme distress facing the empire's full strength, their defeat can be awaited standing—yet what is not yet knowable lies in whether Your Majesty decides or does not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, three prefectures already ruined and exhausted cannot stand against the full power of the empire; their defeat may be awaited at once. What remains unknown is whether Your Majesty will resolve to act.

sentences.zh: 夫兵不多不足以取勝，必勝之師利在速戰，兵多而戰不速則所費必廣。

translations.literal: Troops that are not numerous are insufficient to secure victory; an army certain to win profits from swift battle; if troops are many yet battle is not swift, the expenditure must be vast.
translations.idiomatic: Too few troops cannot win; an army sure of victory must fight swiftly; if the army is large yet the fighting drags on, the cost will be enormous.

sentences.zh: 疆場之上，日相攻劫，近賊州縣，賦役百端，小遇水旱，百姓愁苦。

translations.literal: On the borders they attack and plunder each other daily; in counties near the rebels, levies and corvée multiply in every form; at the slightest flood or drought the common people are afflicted with sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier they raid one another daily; in counties near the rebels taxes and corvée multiply endlessly; at the slightest flood or drought the people are plunged into misery.

sentences.zh: 方此時，人人異議以惑陛下，陛下持之不堅，半塗而罷，傷威損費，為弊必深。

translations.literal: At this time everyone offers differing opinions to confuse Your Majesty; if Your Majesty holds firm without resolution and stops halfway, authority is wounded and expense lost—the harm must be deep.
translations.idiomatic: At such a moment everyone offers conflicting advice to confuse Your Majesty; if Your Majesty does not hold firm and abandons the campaign halfway, imperial prestige will suffer, costs will mount, and the harm will be profound.

sentences.zh: 所要先決於心，詳度本末，事至不惑，乃可圖功。

translations.literal: What is essential is first to decide in the heart, carefully weigh root and branch, so that when matters arrive you are not confused—only then can achievement be planned.
translations.idiomatic: What matters first is to settle the matter in your own mind, weigh root and branch carefully, and face events without wavering—only then can success be sought.

sentences.zh: 又言：「諸道兵羈旅單弱不足用，而界賊州縣，百姓習戰鬥，知賊深淺，若募以內軍，教不三月，一切可用。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The troops of the various circuits, as sojourners, are solitary and weak and insufficient for use; but in counties bordering the rebels the common people are practiced in battle and know the rebels' depth and shallowness—if recruited into the inner army and taught for less than three months, all can be used."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "The troops from the various circuits are strangers here, isolated and weak, and of little use; but in counties on the rebel border the people are seasoned in fighting and know the enemy's strengths and weaknesses. If recruited into the central army and trained for less than three months, they would all be fit for service."

sentences.zh: 又欲「四道置兵，道率三萬，畜力伺利，一日俱縱，則蔡首尾不救，可以責功」。

translations.literal: He also wished "to station troops on four routes, each route leading thirty thousand, storing strength and watching for advantage; released all on one day, then Cai's head and tail could not rescue each other, and merit could be demanded."
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed "posting troops on four routes, thirty thousand men per route, gathering strength and waiting for the right moment; if all were unleashed on a single day, Cai could not rescue both ends at once, and victory could be secured."

sentences.zh: 執政不喜。

translations.literal: Those in power were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers were displeased.

sentences.zh: 會有人詆愈在江陵時為裴均所厚，均子鍔素無狀，愈為文章，字命鍔謗語囂暴，由是改太子右庶子。

translations.literal: It happened that someone slandered Yu, saying that when he was at Jiangling he had been treated generously by Pei Jun; Jun's son E had always been without proper conduct—Yu had written compositions in which, in effect naming E, slanderous words were violently arrogant—and on this account he was changed to Right Subordinate of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Then someone accused Yu of having been favored by Pei Jun while at Jiangling. Jun's son E was notoriously ill-behaved; Yu had written pieces that, though naming E only obliquely, contained violent slanderous language—whereupon Yu was reassigned as Right Subordinate of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 及度以宰相節度彰義軍，宣慰淮西，奏愈行軍司馬。

translations.literal: When Du, as Chancellor, took command of the Zhangyi army as military commissioner and went as imperial envoy to pacify Huai West, he memorialized that Yu serve as army marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du, serving as Chancellor, assumed command of the Zhangyi army and went as imperial envoy to pacify Huai West, he recommended Han Yu as army marshal on the campaign staff.

sentences.zh: 愈請乘遽先入汴，說韓弘使葉力。

translations.literal: Yu requested to ride post-horses and enter Bian first, to persuade Han Hong to exert full strength.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu asked to ride express relays ahead into Bian to urge Han Hong to throw his full weight behind the effort.

sentences.zh: 元濟平，遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Yuanji was pacified, he was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Yuanji was defeated, Han Yu was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 憲宗遣使者往鳳翔迎佛骨入禁中，三日，乃送佛祠。

translations.literal: Xianzong sent envoys to Fengxiang to welcome the Buddha bone into the inner palace; after three days it was sent to the Buddhist shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong sent envoys to Fengxiang to escort the Buddha's finger bone into the palace; three days later it was sent on to the Buddhist shrine.

sentences.zh: 王公士人奔走膜唄，至為夷法，灼體膚，委珍貝，騰遝系路。

translations.literal: Nobles, officials, and scholars ran to join palms in worship; some went so far as barbarian practices, burning their flesh, casting away precious shells, crowding and packing the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Court nobles and literati rushed to worship with joined palms; some adopted foreign rites, burning their flesh and casting jewels and cowries as offerings, until the roads were jammed with surging crowds.

sentences.zh: 愈聞惡之，乃上表曰：

translations.literal: When Yu heard of this he detested it and submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu was revolted on hearing of it and submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 佛者，夷狄之一法耳。

translations.literal: The Buddha is merely one teaching of the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism is only one doctrine among the barbarian peoples.

sentences.zh: 自後漢時始入中國，上古未嘗有也。

translations.literal: Since the Later Han it began to enter China; in high antiquity it never existed.
translations.idiomatic: It entered China only in Later Han times; antiquity never knew it.

sentences.zh: 昔黃帝在位百年，年百一十歲；

translations.literal: In antiquity the Yellow Emperor reigned one hundred years and lived to one hundred ten;
translations.idiomatic: In remote antiquity the Yellow Emperor reigned a hundred years and lived to a hundred and ten;

sentences.zh: 少昊在位八十年，年百歲；

translations.literal: Shaohao reigned eighty years and lived to one hundred;
translations.idiomatic: Shaohao reigned eighty years and lived to a hundred;

sentences.zh: 顓頊在位七十九年，年九十歲；

translations.literal: Zhuanxu reigned seventy-nine years and lived to ninety;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanxu reigned seventy-nine years and lived to ninety;

sentences.zh: 帝嚳在位七十年，年百五歲；

translations.literal: Emperor Ku reigned seventy years and lived to one hundred five;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ku reigned seventy years and lived to a hundred and five;

sentences.zh: 堯在位九十八年，年百一十八歲；

translations.literal: Yao reigned ninety-eight years and lived to one hundred eighteen;
translations.idiomatic: Yao reigned ninety-eight years and lived to a hundred and eighteen;

sentences.zh: 帝舜在位及禹年皆百歲。

translations.literal: Emperor Shun in office and Yu in years each reached one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shun in office and Yu in years each reached a hundred.

sentences.zh: 此時天下太平，百姓安樂壽考，然而中國未有佛也。

translations.literal: At that time all under heaven was at peace, the common people enjoyed ease and long life—yet China had no Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: In those ages the realm was at peace and the people lived long in security—yet China had no Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 其後，湯亦年百歲，湯孫太戊在位七十五年，武丁在位五十年，書史不言其壽，推其年數，蓋不減百歲。

translations.literal: Afterward Tang also lived one hundred years; Tang's grandson Taiwu reigned seventy-five years, Wuding fifty years—the histories do not state their lifespans, but reckoning their years, they surely were not less than one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tang of Shang also lived a hundred years; his grandson Taiwu reigned seventy-five years and Wuding fifty—the annals do not record their ages, but by any count they can hardly have been less than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 周文王年九十七歲，武王年九十三歲，穆王在位百年。

translations.literal: King Wen of Zhou lived ninety-seven years, King Wu ninety-three, King Mu reigned one hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen of Zhou lived ninety-seven years, King Wu ninety-three, and King Mu reigned a hundred years.

sentences.zh: 此時佛法亦未至中國，非因事佛而致然也。

translations.literal: At this time the Buddhist dharma had not yet reached China; it was not because of serving Buddha that this was so.
translations.idiomatic: In that era the Buddhist teaching had not yet reached China; their longevity was not owed to worship of Buddha.

sentences.zh: 漢明帝時始有佛法，明帝在位才十八年。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming of Han's time Buddhism first appeared; Ming reigned only eighteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism first appeared under Emperor Ming of Han, who reigned only eighteen years.

sentences.zh: 其後亂亡相繼，運祚不長。

translations.literal: After that turmoil and ruin followed in succession; their fortune was not long.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter turmoil and ruin followed one upon another, and their dynastic fortunes were brief.

sentences.zh: 宋、齊、梁、陳、元魏以下，事佛漸謹，年代尤促。

translations.literal: From Song, Qi, Liang, Chen, and Northern Wei downward, as they served Buddha with increasing reverence, their reigns grew especially short.
translations.idiomatic: From the Song, Qi, Liang, Chen, and Northern Wei dynasties onward, the more devoutly rulers served Buddhism, the briefer their reigns became.

sentences.zh: 唯梁武帝在位四十八年，前後三捨身施佛，宗廟祭不用牲牢，晝日一食，止於菜果，後為侯景所逼，餓死台城，國亦尋滅。

translations.literal: Only Liang Wudi reigned forty-eight years; thrice he abdicated the throne to donate to the Buddha, temple sacrifices used no livestock, by day one meal limited to vegetables and fruit—later he was driven by Hou Jing, starved to death at Terrace City, and the state soon perished.
translations.idiomatic: Only Emperor Wu of Liang reigned forty-eight years; three times he yielded the throne to fund the sangha, state sacrifices went without animal victims, and he ate but one vegetarian meal a day—until Hou Jing forced him, he starved to death at Terrace City, and the dynasty soon fell.

sentences.zh: 事佛求福，乃更得禍。

translations.literal: Seeking fortune through Buddha instead brought calamity.
translations.idiomatic: To seek blessing through Buddha was only to invite disaster.

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，佛不足信，亦可知矣。

translations.literal: From this one sees that Buddha is not worthy of faith; this also may be known.
translations.idiomatic: From this it is plain that Buddhism is not to be trusted—and that much is already clear.

sentences.zh: 高祖始受隋禪，則議除之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu first received the abdication from Sui, he discussed abolishing it.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu first took the throne from the Sui, he debated abolishing Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 當時君臣識見不遠，不能深究先王之道、古今之宜，推闡聖明，以救斯弊，其事遂止。

translations.literal: At that time the ruler and ministers' understanding did not reach far; they could not deeply investigate the ways of the former kings and what suited past and present, extend sagely clarity to save this abuse—and the matter then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The court's vision then was short; unable to probe deeply the ways of the ancient kings and the needs of their own age, they failed to extend enlightened policy to remedy the evil, and the effort was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 臣常恨焉！

translations.literal: Your servant has often resented this!
translations.idiomatic: I have long bitterly regretted it!

sentences.zh: 伏惟睿聖文武皇帝陛下，神聖英武，數千百年以來，未有倫比。

translations.literal: Bowing my head: Your sagely, martial, civil emperor—sacred and heroic, for thousands of years without equal.
translations.idiomatic: I bow my head: Your Majesty, sage, martial, and cultured—sacred and heroic, without peer in thousands of years.

sentences.zh: 即位之初，即不許度人為僧尼、道士，又不許別立寺觀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of your reign you did not permit ordination as monk or nun or Daoist priest, nor the founding of new temples.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of your reign you forbade new ordinations of monks, nuns, and Daoist priests and the building of new temples.

sentences.zh: 臣當時以為高祖之志，必行于陛下。

translations.literal: Your servant then thought that Gaozu's intent would surely be carried out under Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I then believed that Gaozu's purpose would surely be fulfilled under Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 今縱未能即行，豈可恣之令盛也！

translations.literal: Now, though you cannot act at once, how can you let it flourish unrestrained!
translations.idiomatic: Even if you cannot act at once, how can you let it run wild and flourish!

sentences.zh: 今陛下令群僧迎佛骨於鳳翔，禦樓以觀，舁入大內，又令諸寺遞加供養。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty orders the monks to welcome the Buddha bone from Fengxiang, to view it from the imperial tower, to carry it into the inner palace, and to order the temples to supply offerings in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has ordered monks to welcome the Buddha bone from Fengxiang, to view it from the imperial tower, to carry it into the inner palace, and to have every temple supply offerings in turn.

sentences.zh: 臣雖至愚，必知陛下不惑于佛，作此崇奉以祈福祥也。

translations.literal: Though your servant is extremely foolish, he must know that Your Majesty is not deluded by Buddha and does this reverence to seek blessed fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Foolish though I am, I know Your Majesty is not duped by Buddhism and does not perform this worship to seek fortune.

sentences.zh: 直以豐年之樂，徇人之心，為京都士庶設詭異之觀、戲玩之具耳。

translations.literal: It is simply because of the joy of an abundant year, indulging people's hearts, setting strange sights and playthings for the gentry of the capital—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: It is only the pleasure of a bountiful year, indulging popular sentiment, staging marvels and diversions for the capital's elite—that is all.

sentences.zh: 安有聖明若此，而肯信此等事哉？

translations.literal: How could there be such sagacity and yet believe such things?
translations.idiomatic: How could such sagacity believe such things?

sentences.zh: 然百姓愚冥，易惑難曉，苟見陛下如此，將謂真心信佛，皆云：「天子大聖，猶一心信向；

translations.literal: Yet the common people are dull and benighted, easy to confuse and hard to enlighten; if they see Your Majesty thus they will say you truly believe in Buddha, all declaring: "The Son of Heaven, great sage, still devotes his heart single-mindedly;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the people are benighted, quick to be misled and slow to understand; if they see Your Majesty act thus they will take it for true faith, saying: "The Son of Heaven, himself a great sage, still gives his whole heart to Buddhism;

sentences.zh: 百姓微賤，于佛豈合更惜身命？」

translations.literal: we common people, low and slight—how could we spare body and life before Buddha?"
translations.idiomatic: how can we humble folk cling to our bodies and lives?"

sentences.zh: 以至灼頂燔指，十百為群，解衣散錢，自朝至暮，轉相仿效，唯恐後時，老幼奔波，棄其生業。

translations.literal: —leading to burning scalps and fingers, groups of tens and hundreds, shedding clothes and scattering money from dawn to dusk, copying one another in turn, fearing to be late; old and young ran about and abandoned their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: —until men burn their scalps and fingers in crowds of tens and hundreds, strip off clothing and scatter coin from dawn till dusk, each imitating the next for fear of lagging behind, while young and old rush about and abandon their trades.

sentences.zh: 若不即加禁遏，更曆諸寺，必有斷臂臠身以為供養者。

translations.literal: If this is not immediately forbidden, as it passes through the temples there will surely be those who cut off arms and flesh for offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Unless this is stopped at once, as the relic tours the temples there will surely be those who hack off arms and flesh as offerings.

sentences.zh: 傷風敗俗，傳笑四方，非細事也。

translations.literal: It wounds custom and corrupts mores; ridicule will spread to the four quarters—not a small matter.
translations.idiomatic: It will corrupt custom and invite mockery throughout the realm—no small affair.

sentences.zh: 佛本夷狄之人，與中國言語不通，衣服殊制；

translations.literal: Buddha was originally a man of the barbarians; his speech does not match China's, his dress is of another kind;
translations.idiomatic: Buddha was originally a barbarian: his language is not ours, his dress alien;

sentences.zh: 口不道先王之法言，身不服先王之法服，不知君臣之義、父子之情。

translations.literal: his mouth does not speak the classic words of the former kings, his body does not wear the ritual garments of the former kings, and he does not know the propriety between ruler and minister or the affection between father and son.
translations.idiomatic: his mouth does not utter the teachings of the ancient kings, his body does not wear their ritual garb, and he knows neither the duties of ruler and subject nor the bonds of father and son.

sentences.zh: 假如其身尚在，奉其國命來朝京師，陛下容而接之，不過宣政一見，禮賓一設，賜衣一襲，衛而出之於境，不令貳於眾也。

translations.literal: Suppose his person were still alive and, bearing his state's command, came to the capital—Your Majesty might tolerate and receive him, but it would be no more than one audience in Xuane Hall, one reception in the Host of Guests office, one gift of robes, and an escort beyond the border, not permitting him to lodge among the masses.
translations.idiomatic: If he were alive today and came to court on his ruler's orders, Your Majesty might receive him—but only for one audience in Xuane Hall, one banquet in the Host of Guests office, one gift of robes, and an escort beyond the frontier, never allowing him to dwell among the people.

sentences.zh: 況其身死已久，枯朽之骨，凶穢之餘，豈宜以入宮禁？

translations.literal: How much more when his body has long been dead—a withered bone, a remnant of evil filth: how can it enter the palace precincts?
translations.idiomatic: How much less should his long-dead body—withered bone, foul and unclean remnant—be brought within the palace?

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「敬鬼神而遠之。」

translations.literal: Confucius said: "Respect the spirits and gods, yet keep them at a distance."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "Respect the spirits, yet keep them at a distance."

sentences.zh: 古之諸侯吊于其國，必令巫祝先以桃茢祓除不祥，然後進吊。

translations.literal: When the feudal lords of old offered condolences in a state, they always ordered the shamans first to exorcise with peach wands and reed mats, and only then proceeded with the condolence.
translations.idiomatic: When ancient feudal lords offered condolences abroad, they always had shamans purify the way with peach wands and reed brushes before entering to mourn.

sentences.zh: 今無故取朽穢之物，親臨觀之，巫祝不先，桃茢不用，君臣不言其非，御史不舉其失，臣實恥之。

translations.literal: Now, without cause, a rotten, filthy object is taken and personally viewed; no shamans go before, no peach wands or reeds are used; ruler and ministers do not speak of the wrong, censors do not report the fault—your servant is truly shamed.
translations.idiomatic: Now a foul and rotten thing is fetched for Your Majesty to view in person; no shamans precede it, no peach wands or reed brushes are employed; neither court nor censors protest the offense—and I am deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 乞以此骨付之水火，永絕根本，斷天下之疑，絕前代之惑，使天下之人知大聖人之所作為，出於尋常萬萬也。

translations.literal: I beg that this bone be handed to fire and water, eternally cutting the root, ending doubt under heaven, cutting off the delusion of former ages, so that all under heaven may know the great sage's conduct surpasses the ordinary ten thousandfold.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that this bone be committed to fire and water, root and branch destroyed forever, all doubt under heaven ended and the delusions of past ages cut off, so that the people may know Your Majesty's deeds rise immeasurably above the common run.

sentences.zh: 佛如有靈，能作禍祟，凡有殃咎，宜加臣身。

translations.literal: If Buddha has a spirit and can bring calamity, any ill fortune should be visited on my person.
translations.idiomatic: If the Buddha has power to bring harm, let every misfortune fall on me alone.

sentences.zh: 上天鑒臨，臣不怨悔。

translations.literal: Heaven oversees; your servant harbors no resentment or regret.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is my witness; I shall bear no resentment or regret.

sentences.zh: 表入，帝大怒，持示宰相，將抵以死。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor was greatly angry, showed it to the chancellors, and was about to punish him with death.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor was furious, showed it to his chancellors, and was ready to put him to death.

sentences.zh: 裴度、崔群曰：「愈言訐牾，罪之誠宜。

translations.literal: Pei Du and Cui Qun said: "Yu's words are confronting and blunt; punishment is truly fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du and Cui Qun said: "Han Yu's language is confrontational and offensive; he deserves punishment.

sentences.zh: 然非內懷至忠，安能及此？

translations.literal: Yet if he did not harbor utmost loyalty within, how could he have gone so far?
translations.idiomatic: Yet unless he were utterly loyal at heart, how could he have dared so much?

sentences.zh: 願少寬假，以來諫爭。」

translations.literal: We beg a little leniency to encourage remonstrance."
translations.idiomatic: We beg Your Majesty to show a little mercy, that remonstrance may not be discouraged."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「愈言我奉佛太過，猶可容；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Yu said I revere Buddha too much—that can be tolerated;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "When Han Yu said I revered Buddhism too deeply, that I could bear;

sentences.zh: 至謂東漢奉佛以後，天子感夭促，言何乖剌邪？

translations.literal: but to go so far as to say that after the Eastern Han served Buddha, emperors felt their lives shortened—how contrary and piercing is that!
translations.idiomatic: but to claim that since the Eastern Han worshipped Buddha, emperors' lives have been cut short—how perverse and wounding is that!

sentences.zh: 愈，人臣，狂妄敢爾，固不可赦！」

translations.literal: Yu, a subject, arrogant and daring thus—solidly he cannot be pardoned!"
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu, a mere subject, dares such insolence—he truly cannot be forgiven!"

sentences.zh: 於是中外駭懼，雖戚裏諸貴，亦為愈言，乃貶潮州刺史。

translations.literal: Then inside and outside were terrified; even the imperial kin and nobles spoke for Yu, and he was demoted to prefect of Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: At this the court and country were alarmed; even imperial relatives pleaded for him, and he was demoted to prefect of Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 既至潮，以表哀謝曰：

translations.literal: When he reached Chao, he submitted a memorial of grief and apology, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Chaozhou he submitted a memorial of repentance, which read:

sentences.zh: 臣以狂妄戇愚，不識禮度，陳佛骨事，言涉不恭，正名定罪，萬死莫塞。

translations.literal: Your servant, through arrogant, reckless folly, did not know ritual propriety; in the matter of the Buddha bone his words touched on disrespect; judged by the rectification of names, ten thousand deaths could not atone.
translations.idiomatic: I, through arrogant folly and reckless ignorance of ritual, spoke disrespectfully on the Buddha bone; by the standards of law and duty, ten thousand deaths would not suffice.

sentences.zh: 陛下哀臣愚忠，恕臣狂直，謂言雖可罪，心亦無他，特屈刑章，以臣為潮州刺史。

translations.literal: Your Majesty pitied your servant's foolish loyalty, forgave his reckless bluntness, saying that though the words might be criminal the heart held no other intent, and specially bent the penal code to appoint him prefect of Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty pitied my foolish loyalty, forgave my blunt rashness, held that though my words were culpable my heart was innocent, and mercifully bent the law to make me prefect of Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 既免刑誅，又獲祿食，聖恩寬大，天地莫量，破腦刳心，豈足為謝！

translations.literal: Having escaped execution and also received salary, the sage grace is vast beyond measure of heaven and earth; to split brain and carve heart could not suffice for thanks!
translations.idiomatic: Spared execution and granted a stipend—Your grace is wider than heaven and earth; were I to rend my skull and lay bare my heart, it could not repay you!

sentences.zh: 臣所領州，在廣府極東，過海口，下惡水，濤瀧壯猛，難計期程，颶風鱷魚，患禍不測。

translations.literal: The prefecture your servant leads lies at the eastern extremity of Guang prefecture; beyond Haikou one descends evil waters where billows and rapids are violent and the journey cannot be reckoned; hurricanes and crocodiles bring perils beyond foresight.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture I govern lies at the far eastern edge of Guang; beyond Haikou lie foul waters where surges and rapids are fierce and the route cannot be timed; typhoons and crocodiles bring perils no man can foresee.

sentences.zh: 州南近界，漲海連天，毒霧瘴氛，日夕發作。

translations.literal: South of the prefecture the border is near; the swollen sea joins the sky, and poisonous mists and miasma break out morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: South of the prefecture the frontier presses close; the swollen sea meets the sky, and poisonous vapors and miasma rise morning and night.

sentences.zh: 臣少多病，年才五十，發白齒落，理不久長。

translations.literal: Your servant from youth has been often ill; his years have only reached fifty, his hair white and teeth fallen—his span cannot be long.
translations.idiomatic: I have been sickly since youth; I am only fifty, my hair white and teeth gone—my days cannot be many.

sentences.zh: 加以罪犯至重，所處遠惡，憂惶慚悸，死亡無日。

translations.literal: Added to this, his crime is extremely grave and his post remote and vile; in anxious fear and shameful dread, death has no distant day.
translations.idiomatic: Add to this a grave offense and a remote, hostile post, and I live in anxious shame with death ever near.

sentences.zh: 單立一身，朝無親党，居蠻夷之地，與魑魅同群，苟非陛下哀而念之，誰肯為臣言者？

translations.literal: Standing alone without kin at court, dwelling in barbarian lands among demons and sprites—if not for Your Majesty's pity and remembrance, who would speak for your servant?
translations.idiomatic: Alone, without allies at court, I dwell in barbarian country among demons—were it not for Your Majesty's pity, who would plead for me?

sentences.zh: 臣受性愚陋，人事多所不通，惟酷好學問文章，未嘗一日暫廢，實為時輩所見推許。

translations.literal: Your servant's nature is stupid and crude; in human affairs he is much unskilled—only he bitterly loves learning and literature and has never ceased a single day; this is truly what his contemporaries praise and acknowledge.
translations.idiomatic: My nature is dull and awkward, and I am unversed in worldly affairs—only in scholarship and letters have I never ceased a single day, and this my peers have acknowledged.

sentences.zh: 臣于當時之文，亦未有過人者。

translations.literal: In the literature of the time your servant also had no one surpassing him.
translations.idiomatic: Among the writers of my day I was not without standing.

sentences.zh: 至於論述陛下功德，與《詩》、《書》相表裏，作為歌詩，薦之郊廟，紀太山之封，鏤白玉之牒，鋪張對天之宏休，揚厲無前之偉績，編於《詩》、《書》之策而無愧，措於天地之間而無虧，雖使古人復生，臣未肯讓。

translations.literal: As for discoursing on Your Majesty's merit and virtue in parallel with the Odes and Documents, composing songs and hymns to present at the suburban altars, recording the feng on Mount Tai, inscribing the white-jade tablet, spreading abroad the grand blessing that faces Heaven, and exalting unprecedented mighty achievement—if compiled in the policies of the Odes and Documents he would not be ashamed, set between heaven and earth he would not be wanting; even if the ancients were revived, your servant would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: But to expound Your Majesty's merit and virtue in words worthy of the Odes and Documents, to compose hymns for the suburban sacrifices, to record a feng on Mount Tai and inscribe the jade tablet, to proclaim blessings that face Heaven and achievements without precedent in history—texts fit for the Book of Songs and Documents without shame, deeds that stand between heaven and earth without fault—even were the ancients restored to life, I would not yield.

sentences.zh: 伏以皇唐受命有天下，四海之內，莫不臣妾，南北東西，地各萬里。

translations.literal: Bowing my head: the August Tang received the Mandate and possessed all under heaven; within the four seas none failed to be subject; north, south, east, and west—each region ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: I bow my head: when great Tang received the Mandate, it ruled all within the seas; to every quarter of the earth, ten thousand li in extent, none failed to submit.

sentences.zh: 自天寶以後，政治少懈，文致未優，武克不剛，孽臣奸隸，蠹居棋處，搖毒自防，外順內悖，父死子代，以祖以孫，如古諸侯，自擅其地，不朝不貢，六七十年。

translations.literal: From the Tianbao era onward, government grew somewhat lax, civil polish was not yet perfected, martial prowess not yet firm; wicked ministers and treacherous underlings, like vermin on a chessboard, shook poison to guard themselves, outwardly compliant yet inwardly rebellious; father died and son succeeded, grandson after grandfather, like the feudal lords of old each usurping his territory, neither attending court nor paying tribute—for sixty or seventy years.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tianbao, governance slackened, culture was not yet refined nor arms fully restored; treacherous ministers nested like worms on a board, hoarding poison to shield themselves, compliant without yet rebel within; fathers died and sons inherited, grandsons followed grandfathers, like ancient feudal lords seizing their own domains, neither attending court nor paying tribute—for sixty or seventy years.

sentences.zh: 四聖傳序，以至陛下。

translations.literal: Four sage emperors passed the succession in order down to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Four sage rulers handed down the succession until Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位以來，躬親聽斷，旋乾轉坤，關機闔開，雷厲風飛，日月清照，天戈所麾，無不從順。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne you have personally heard cases and decided them, turning heaven and earth as on a pivot, opening and closing the keys of power; thunderclap and wind-flight, sun and moon clear in illumination; wherever the heavenly halberd pointed, none failed to comply.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty took the throne you have personally judged affairs, turning the cosmos on its pivot, opening and closing the gates of power; like thunder and wind you have swept the realm, sun and moon shining clear; wherever the imperial arms have pointed, none has failed to obey.

sentences.zh: 宜定樂章，以告神明，東巡泰山，奏功皇天，具著顯庸，明示得意，使永永年服我成烈。

translations.literal: It is fitting to fix ritual music and report to the spirits, to tour east to Mount Tai, present achievement to August Heaven, make manifest outstanding merit, show clearly your satisfaction, and cause generation after generation forever to serve your great accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: You should fix the ritual music and announce it to the gods, tour east to Mount Tai, present your achievements to Heaven, display your merit in full, declare your triumph, and make all ages forever serve your great accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 當此之際，所謂千載一時不可逢之嘉會，而臣負罪嬰釁，自拘海島，戚戚嗟嗟，日與死迫，曾不得奏薄伎於從官之內、隸禦之間，窮思畢精，以贖前過。

translations.literal: At such a time it is what is called a thousand-year occasion that cannot be encountered twice; yet your servant, bearing guilt and offense, confines himself on a sea-island, sorrowful and sighing, day by day pressed by death, never able to present his slight skill among attendant officials and within the imperial retinue, exhausting thought and utmost refinement to redeem former faults.
translations.idiomatic: At such a moment—what men call a once-in-a-thousand-years opportunity—I, guilty and disgraced, am confined on a distant shore, grieving day by day toward death, unable to offer my poor talents among your attendants and within the imperial household, to pour out all my mind and redeem my fault.

sentences.zh: 懷痛窮天，死不閉目，伏惟陛下天地父母，哀而憐之。

translations.literal: Bearing pain that reaches to heaven, in death his eyes would not close; bowing my head: Your Majesty, heaven and earth and parents—pity and cherish your servant.
translations.idiomatic: My grief reaches to heaven; I could not die with closed eyes. I bow my head: Your Majesty, my heaven and earth, my father and mother—pity me and show mercy.

sentences.zh: 帝得表，頗感悔，欲復用之，持示宰相曰：「愈前所論是大愛朕，然不當言天子事佛乃年促耳。」

translations.literal: When the emperor received the memorial he was quite moved to regret and wished to employ him again; he showed it to the chancellors, saying: "Yu's former discourse was from great love of Us, yet he ought not to have said that emperors who served Buddha had shortened lives."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor received the memorial he was deeply moved and wished to recall him; he showed it to the chancellors, saying: "Han Yu's earlier remonstrance sprang from great love for me, yet he should not have said that emperors who served Buddhism lived short lives."

sentences.zh: 皇甫鎛素忌愈直，即奏言：「愈終狂疏，可且內移。」

translations.literal: Huangfu Bo had long resented Yu's bluntness and at once memorialized, saying: "Yu is ultimately wild and reckless; he may for the present be moved inward."
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Bo, who had long resented Han Yu's outspokenness, immediately memorialized: "Han Yu remains incorrigibly rash; for now he may be transferred closer to the capital."

sentences.zh: 乃改袁州刺史。

translations.literal: He was then changed to prefect of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu was then reassigned as prefect of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，愈至潮州，問民疾苦，皆曰：「惡溪有鱷魚，食民畜產且盡，民以是窮。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yu reached Chaozhou, he inquired into the people's hardships; all said: "In Evil Creek there are crocodiles that devour the people's livestock until none is left, and the people are therefore destitute."
translations.idiomatic: When Han Yu first reached Chaozhou, he asked about the people's hardships; all said: "Evil Creek holds crocodiles that devour livestock until nothing is left, and the people are ruined thereby."

sentences.zh: 數日，愈自往視之，令其屬秦濟以一羊一豚投溪水而祝之曰：

translations.literal: Several days later Yu went in person to view it; he ordered his subordinate Qin Ji to cast a sheep and a pig into the creek water and offered this prayer:
translations.idiomatic: Days later Han Yu went to see for himself; he had his aide Qin Ji cast a sheep and a pig into the creek and pronounced this address:

sentences.zh: 昔先王既有天下，列山澤，罔繩擉刃以除蟲蛇惡物為民物害者，驅而出之四海之外。

translations.literal: In antiquity the former kings, having possessed all under heaven, marked off mountains and marshes, spread nets and deployed blades to remove insects, serpents, and harmful creatures for the people's goods, and drove them out beyond the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when the former kings possessed the realm, they marked mountains and marshes, spread nets and bared blades to rid the land of insects, serpents, and creatures harmful to the people, and drove them out beyond the four seas.

sentences.zh: 及德薄，不能遠有，則江、漢之間尚皆棄之以與蠻夷楚越，況湖、嶺之間去京師萬里哉？

translations.literal: When virtue grew thin and they could not hold distant regions, even between the Yangtze and Han they still abandoned territory to the Man, Yi, Chu, and Yue—how much more the region between the lakes and the ranges, ten thousand li from the capital!
translations.idiomatic: When virtue waned and distant lands could not be held, even between the Yangtze and Han they yielded ground to the southern tribes—how much more this country between lake and range, ten thousand li from the capital!

sentences.zh: 鱷魚之涵淹卵育於此，亦固其所。

translations.literal: That crocodiles soak and breed their eggs here is also, solidly, where they belong.
translations.idiomatic: That crocodiles breed and dwell here is, after all, only fitting.

sentences.zh: 今天子嗣唐位，神聖慈武，四海之外，六合之內，皆撫而有之，況禹跡所掩，揚州之近地，刺史縣令之所治，出貢賦以供天地、宗廟、百神之祀之壤者哉？

translations.literal: Today the Son of Heaven has succeeded to the Tang throne, sacred, merciful, and martial; beyond the four seas, within the six directions, all are comforted and possessed—how much more lands within the trace of Yu, ground near Yangzhou, soil governed by prefect and magistrate, bearing tribute for the sacrifices of heaven and earth, the ancestral temples, and the hundred spirits!
translations.idiomatic: Today the Son of Heaven has inherited Tang, sacred, merciful, and martial; beyond the four seas and within the six realms all are ruled—how much less should this land within Yu's footprint, this ground near Yangzhou, this soil of prefects and magistrates that pays tribute for the rites of Heaven, Earth, the ancestors, and the hundred spirits, harbor such creatures!

sentences.zh: 鱷魚其不可與刺史雜處此土也。

translations.literal: The crocodile cannot share this soil with the prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The crocodile cannot share this soil with the prefect.

sentences.zh: 刺史受天子命，守此土，治此民，而鱷魚旰然不安溪潭據處，食民畜熊豕鹿麞以肥其身，以種其子孫，與刺史拒爭為長雄。

translations.literal: The prefect receives the Son of Heaven's command to guard this soil and govern these people, yet the crocodile glares and will not rest in the pool and deep, occupying the place, eating the people's livestock—bears, pigs, deer, and roebuck—to fatten its body and breed its offspring, contending with the prefect for mastery as a great champion.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect bears the Son of Heaven's commission to guard this land and govern these people, yet the crocodile glares from the deep, devouring cattle, swine, deer, and roebuck to fatten itself and breed its young, contending with the prefect as a rival chieftain.

sentences.zh: 刺史雖駑弱，亦安肯為鱷魚低首下心，伈々睍斯，為吏民羞，以偷活於此也？

translations.literal: Though the prefect is weak and timid, how could he willingly bow his head and humble his heart, cringing and fawning, shaming officials and people to steal life here?
translations.idiomatic: Weak and timid though the prefect may be, how could he bow his head, cringe and fawn, and shame his officers and people merely to cling to life here?

sentences.zh: 承天子命以來為吏，固其勢不得不與鱷魚辨。

translations.literal: Receiving the Son of Heaven's command to come as an official, by the force of circumstance he cannot but contend with the crocodile.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioned by the Son of Heaven to govern, by duty I must dispute with the crocodile.

sentences.zh: 鱷魚有知，其聽刺史。

translations.literal: If the crocodile has understanding, let it heed the prefect.
translations.idiomatic: If the crocodile has sense, let it heed the prefect.

sentences.zh: 潮之州，大海在其南，鯨鵬之大，蝦蟹之細，無不容歸，以生以食，鱷魚朝發而夕至也。

translations.literal: The prefecture of Chao: the great sea lies to its south; whales and peng-birds great, shrimp and crabs small—all without exception may return, living by what the sea provides; the crocodile can set out at dawn and arrive by evening.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozhou lies beside the sea: to the south the ocean holds all, from leviathans to the smallest shrimp; all may dwell there and find food. A crocodile can leave at dawn and be there by evening.

sentences.zh: 今與鱷魚約：「盡三日，其率丑類南徙於海，以避天子之命吏。

translations.literal: Now I make this covenant with the crocodile: "Within three days lead your ugly kind southward to the sea to avoid the Son of Heaven's commissioned officer.
translations.idiomatic: Now I set this covenant with the crocodile: "Within three days lead your kind south to the sea and avoid the Son of Heaven's officer.

sentences.zh: 三日不能，至五日；

translations.literal: If three days are not enough, then five;
translations.idiomatic: If three days are not enough, take five;

sentences.zh: 五日不能，至七日，七日不能，是終不肯徙也，是不有刺史、聽從其言也。

translations.literal: if five are not enough, then seven; if seven are not enough, then you ultimately refuse to move—this is to have no prefect and not heed his words.
translations.idiomatic: if five are not enough, take seven; if seven are not enough, you refuse to move—then you deny the prefect and reject his command.

sentences.zh: 不然，則是鱷魚冥頑不靈，刺史雖有言，不聞不知也。

translations.literal: Otherwise the crocodile is benighted, dull, and without spirit; though the prefect has spoken, it does not hear and does not know.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the crocodile is stupid and without understanding; though the prefect has spoken, you neither hear nor know.

sentences.zh: 夫傲天子之命吏，不聽其言，不徙以避之，與頑不靈而為民物害者，皆可殺。

translations.literal: To defy the Son of Heaven's commissioned officer, not heed his words, not move to avoid him, together with the stupid and spiritless who harm the people's goods—all may be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever defies the Son of Heaven's officer, ignores his words, and will not flee—all such benighted creatures that harm the people may be put to death.

sentences.zh: 刺史則選材技民，操強弓毒矢，以與鱷魚從事，必盡殺乃止，其無悔！」

translations.literal: The prefect will then select skilled men of the district, take strong bows and poisoned arrows, and take the field against the crocodile, killing until none remain—let there be no regret!"
translations.idiomatic: The prefect will choose able men, arm strong bows and poisoned arrows, and make war on the crocodile until all are slain—let there be no remorse!"

sentences.zh: 祝之夕，暴風震電起溪中，數日水盡涸，西徙六十里。

translations.literal: On the evening of the prayer-offering, violent wind, thunder, and lightning arose in the stream; within days the water dried completely, and [the crocodiles] moved west sixty li.
translations.idiomatic: That very night, as the prayers were offered, a violent storm erupted from the stream with thunder and lightning; within days the water ran dry, and [the crocodiles] shifted west sixty li.

sentences.zh: 自是潮無鱷魚患。

translations.literal: From then on, Chaozhou had no crocodile plague.
translations.idiomatic: From that time forward, Chaozhou was free of the crocodile menace.

sentences.zh: 袁人以男女為隸，過期不贖，則沒入之。

translations.literal: The people of Yuan [prefecture] took men and women as slaves; when the redemption period expired without payment, they were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuan prefecture, people held men and women as bond-slaves; if not ransomed by the deadline, they were forfeited to the holder.

sentences.zh: 愈至，悉計庸得贖所沒，歸之父母七百余人。

translations.literal: When Yu arrived, he fully calculated wages to redeem all who had been confiscated, returning more than seven hundred to their parents.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Yu arrived, he calculated wages owed and ransomed every forfeited person, restoring more than seven hundred to their families.

sentences.zh: 因與約，禁其為隸。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made a covenant with them, forbidding [the practice of] taking slaves.
translations.idiomatic: He then entered into agreements forbidding the holding of bond-slaves.

sentences.zh: 召拜國子祭酒，轉兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Director of the Imperial Academy; [he was] transferred to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed Director of the Imperial Academy, then transferred to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 鎮州亂，殺田弘正而立王廷湊，詔愈宣撫。

translations.literal: Zhenzhou rebelled; they killed Tian Hongzheng and installed Wang Tingcou; [the emperor] decreed Yu as pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhou rose in revolt, killing Tian Hongzheng and enthroning Wang Tingcou in his place; the court appointed Han Yu pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 既行，眾皆危之。

translations.literal: Once he had set out, all regarded his position as perilous.
translations.idiomatic: After he departed, everyone feared for his safety.

sentences.zh: 元稹言：「韓愈可惜。」

translations.literal: Yuan Zhen said: "It would be a pity to lose Han Yu."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen remarked, "Han Yu is too valuable to risk."

sentences.zh: 穆宗亦悔，詔愈度事從宜，無必入。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong also regretted [the mission] and decreed that Yu should gauge affairs as circumstances required, without necessarily entering [Zhenzhou].
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong likewise regretted the assignment and ordered Han Yu to handle matters as he saw fit, without insisting that he enter the rebel stronghold.

sentences.zh: 愈至，廷湊嚴兵迓之，甲士陳廷。

translations.literal: When Yu arrived, Tingcou arrayed troops sternly to receive him, armored soldiers lining the court.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Yu arrived, Wang Tingcou met him with troops drawn up in battle order, armored soldiers filling the hall.

sentences.zh: 既坐，廷湊曰：「所以紛紛者，乃此士卒也。」

translations.literal: Once seated, Tingcou said: "Those responsible for all this uproar are precisely these soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: After they were seated, Wang Tingcou said, "These soldiers here are the cause of all the turmoil."

sentences.zh: 愈大聲曰；

translations.literal: Yu said in a loud voice:
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu raised his voice and said:

sentences.zh: 「天子以公為有將帥材，故賜以節，豈意同賊反邪？」

translations.literal: "The Son of Heaven considered you possessed of commander talent, and therefore bestowed the staff of office—did he intend that you join the bandits in rebellion?"
translations.idiomatic: "The Son of Heaven believed you had the makings of a general and gave you the commander's baton—did he mean for you to side with rebels?"

sentences.zh: 語未終，士前奮曰：「先太師為國擊硃滔，血衣猶在，此軍何負，乃以為賊乎？」

translations.literal: Before he finished speaking, soldiers stepped forward vehemently and said: "The former Grand Tutor fought Zhu Tao for the state; his blood-stained garments are still here—what fault has this army, that you call us bandits?"
translations.idiomatic: Before he could finish, soldiers surged forward: "Our late Grand Tutor fought Zhu Tao for the empire—his bloody garments remain! What crime has this army committed, that you brand us rebels?"

sentences.zh: 愈曰：「以為爾不記先太師也，若猶記之，固善。

translations.literal: Yu said: "I had thought you did not remember the former Grand Tutor; if you still remember him, so much the better.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu replied, "I thought you had forgotten your Grand Tutor; if you still honor his memory, all the better.

sentences.zh: 天寶以來，安祿山、史思明、李希烈等有子若孫在乎？

translations.literal: Since the Tianbao era, have An Lushan, Shi Siming, Li Xilie, and the like had sons or grandsons [among you]?
translations.idiomatic: Since the Tianbao era, have the sons or grandsons of An Lushan, Shi Siming, Li Xilie, and their kind survived among you?

sentences.zh: 亦有居官者乎？」

translations.literal: Have any of them held office?"
translations.idiomatic: Did any of them hold government posts?"

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「無。」

translations.literal: The crowd said: "None."
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers answered, "None."

sentences.zh: 愈曰：「田公以魏博六州歸朝廷，官中書令，父子受旗節；

translations.literal: Yu said: "Lord Tian surrendered the six prefectures of Weibo to the court and was appointed Grand Counselor; father and son both received banners and staffs;
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu continued, "Lord Tian surrendered Weibo's six prefectures to the court and rose to Grand Counselor; father and son both received command banners and staffs of office—

sentences.zh: 劉悟、李祐皆大鎮。

translations.literal: Liu Wu and Li You both held great prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wu and Li You each governed major circuits.

sentences.zh: 此爾軍所其聞也。」

translations.literal: This is what your army has surely heard."
translations.idiomatic: These are deeds your army well knows."

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「弘正刻，故此軍不安。」

translations.literal: The crowd said: "Hongzheng was harsh, hence this army was unsettled."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "Hongzheng was severe—that is why the army grew restless."

sentences.zh: 愈曰：「然爾曹亦害田公，又殘其家矣，復何道？」

translations.literal: Yu said: "Yet you yourselves also harmed Lord Tian and further ravaged his household—what more is there to say?"
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu said, "Yet you yourselves killed Lord Tian and destroyed his family—what excuse remains?"

sentences.zh: 眾讙曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The crowd clamored noisily: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers broke into an uproar, crying, "Fair enough!"

sentences.zh: 廷湊慮眾變，疾麾使去。

translations.literal: Tingcou feared the crowd would change, and swiftly waved them to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingcou, fearing the troops might turn, quickly gestured for them to leave.

sentences.zh: 因曰：「今欲廷湊何所為？」

translations.literal: Thereupon he said: "What now does [Wang] Tingcou wish me to do?"
translations.idiomatic: He then asked, "What do you wish Tingcou to do now?"

sentences.zh: 愈曰：「神策六軍將如牛元翼者為不乏，但朝廷顧大體，不可棄之。

translations.literal: Yu said: "Among the Shence Six Armies, commanders such as Niu Yuanyi are not scarce, but the court regards the larger interest and cannot abandon him.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu answered, "The Shence Armies have no lack of generals like Niu Yuanyi, yet the court cares for the larger interest and cannot abandon him.

sentences.zh: 公久圍之，何也？」

translations.literal: You have long besieged him—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Why have you besieged him so long?"

sentences.zh: 廷湊曰：「即出之。」

translations.literal: Tingcou said: "I will release him at once."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingcou said, "I will release him forthwith."

sentences.zh: 愈曰：「若爾，則無事矣。」

translations.literal: Yu said: "If so, then there will be no further trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu said, "Then all will be well."

sentences.zh: 會元翼亦潰圍出，延湊不追。

translations.literal: It happened that Yuanyi also broke the siege and escaped; Tingcou did not pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Niu Yuanyi had already broken out of the encirclement; Wang Tingcou did not give chase.

sentences.zh: 愈歸奏其語，帝大悅。

translations.literal: Yu returned and reported his words; the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu returned and reported what had been said; the emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: [He was] transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時宰相李逢吉惡李紳，欲逐之，遂以愈為京兆尹、兼御史大夫，特詔不台參，而除紳中丞。

translations.literal: At the time, Chief Minister Li Fengji hated Li Shen and wished to expel him; accordingly he made Yu Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, with a special decree exempting him from attending at the Censorate, while appointing Shen Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister Li Fengji detested Li Shen and sought to drive him out. He appointed Han Yu Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, with a special exemption from Censorate audiences, while installing Li Shen as Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 紳果劾奏愈，愈以詔自解。

translations.literal: Shen indeed impeached and memorialized against Yu; Yu excused himself by citing the imperial decree.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen duly impeached Han Yu, who defended himself by citing the special imperial order.

sentences.zh: 其後文刺紛然，宰相以台、府不協，遂罷愈為兵部侍郎，而出紳江西觀察使。

translations.literal: Thereafter written attacks flew back and forth; the chief minister, because the Censorate and the metropolitan office did not harmonize, then removed Yu to Vice Minister of War and sent Shen out as Jiangxi observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials and counter-memorials followed; concluding that the Censorate and the metropolitan government could not work together, the chief minister demoted Han Yu to Vice Minister of War and sent Li Shen out as Jiangxi observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 紳見帝，得留，愈亦復為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Shen saw the emperor, he was permitted to remain; Yu also returned to Vice Minister of Personnel.
