translations.idiomatic: Li Shen gained an audience with the emperor and was allowed to stay; Han Yu likewise resumed his post as Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 長慶四年卒，年五十七，贈禮部尚書，諡曰文。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Changqing he died, aged fifty-seven; he was posthumously granted Minister of Rites, with posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of the Changqing reign (824), at fifty-seven. He was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites, with the posthumous epithet Wen ("Literary").

sentences.zh: 愈性明銳，不詭隨。

translations.literal: Yu's nature was keen and sharp; he did not compromise or go along.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu was sharp and incisive by nature, unwilling to trim his sails or follow the crowd.

sentences.zh: 與人交，始終不少變。

translations.literal: In friendship with others, from beginning to end he scarcely changed.
translations.idiomatic: In his dealings with others, he remained steadfast from first to last.

sentences.zh: 成就後進士，往往知名。

translations.literal: He advanced younger scholars, who often became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He nurtured younger scholars, many of whom achieved fame.

sentences.zh: 經愈指授，皆稱「韓門弟子」，愈官顯，稍謝遣。

translations.literal: Those who received Yu's instruction were all styled "disciples of the Han school"; when Yu's office grew eminent, he gradually dismissed them.
translations.idiomatic: Those he tutored were called "disciples of Master Han's gate"; as his rank rose, he gradually released them from formal patronage.

sentences.zh: 凡內外親若交友無後者，為嫁遣孤女而恤其家。

translations.literal: For all relatives within and without the family, or friends without heirs, he arranged marriages for orphaned daughters and supported their households.
translations.idiomatic: For kin and friends alike who left no heirs, he saw orphan daughters married off and sustained their households.

sentences.zh: 嫂鄭喪，為服期以報。

translations.literal: When his sister-in-law Lady Zheng died, he wore mourning for the full term in requital.
translations.idiomatic: When his sister-in-law the Lady Zheng died, he observed the full mourning period in gratitude for her care.

sentences.zh: 每言文章自漢司馬相如、太史公、劉向、揚雄後，作者不世出，故愈深探本元，卓然樹立，成一家言。

translations.literal: He often said that in prose since Han times' Sima Xiangru, the Grand Historian, Liu Xiang, and Yang Xiong, writers had not appeared generation after generation; therefore Yu deeply probed the root principles, stood forth conspicuously, and formed a school of his own.
translations.idiomatic: He often declared that since the Han masters—Sima Xiangru, Sima Qian, Liu Xiang, and Yang Xiong—literary genius had not appeared every generation; accordingly Han Yu plumbed the deepest sources, established himself with distinction, and founded a literary school of his own.

sentences.zh: 其《原道》、《原性》、《師說》等數十篇，皆奧衍閎深，與孟軻、揚雄相表裏而佐佑《六經》云。

translations.literal: His several tens of pieces such as "Essay on the Way," "Essay on Human Nature," and "On the Teacher" were all profound in substance and vast in scope, forming the inner and outer complement to Mencius and Yang Xiong and supporting the Six Classics.
translations.idiomatic: His treatises—"Essay on the Way," "Essay on Human Nature," "On the Teacher," and dozens more—were profound and capacious, framing and reinforcing the Six Classics as Mencius and Yang Xiong had done.

sentences.zh: 至它文，造端置辭，要為不襲蹈前人者。

translations.literal: As for his other writings, in opening and phrasing, the gist was that he did not tread in the footsteps of predecessors.
translations.idiomatic: In his other compositions, he invariably opened and phrased his work without imitating earlier models.

sentences.zh: 然惟愈為之，沛然若有餘，至其徒李翱、李漢、皇甫湜從而效之，遽不及遠甚。

translations.literal: Yet only Yu could do this with overflowing abundance, as though he had more than enough; when his disciples Li Ao, Li Han, and Huangfu Shi followed and emulated him, they were suddenly far short by comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Only Han Yu could write thus, with effortless abundance; when his disciples Li Ao, Li Han, and Huangfu Shi tried to follow his example, they fell far short at once.

sentences.zh: 從愈游者，若孟郊、張籍，亦皆自名于時。

translations.literal: Those who studied under Yu, such as Meng Jiao and Zhang Ji, each likewise made names for themselves in their time.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who studied with him—Meng Jiao and Zhang Ji, for example—each likewise won renown in his own day.

sentences.zh: 附 孟郊

translations.literal: Appended: Meng Jiao
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Meng Jiao

sentences.zh: 孟郊者，字東野，湖州武康人。

translations.literal: Meng Jiao, styled Dongye, was a native of Wukang in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jiao, courtesy name Dongye, was from Wukang in Huzhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少隱嵩山，性介，少諧合。

translations.literal: In youth he lived in seclusion on Mount Song; his nature was upright and unconforming, seldom harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he lived as a recluse on Mount Song; upright and uncompromising by nature, he mingled poorly with others.

sentences.zh: 愈一見為忘形交。

translations.literal: Upon one meeting, Han Yu took him as a friend beyond formalities.
translations.idiomatic: At their first meeting, Han Yu and he became intimate friends without regard for rank.

sentences.zh: 年五十，得進士第，調溧陽尉。

translations.literal: At age fifty he obtained the jinshi degree and was assigned as magistrate of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: At fifty he finally passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 縣有投金瀨、平陵城，林薄蒙翳，下有積水。

translations.literal: The county had the Toujin Brook and Pingling Citadel, with dense thickets shrouding [the ground], and standing water below.
translations.idiomatic: The county boasted the Toujin Brook and the ruins of Pingling, where dense woods cast deep shade over pools of stagnant water.

sentences.zh: 郊閑往坐水旁，裴回賦詩，而曹務多廢。

translations.literal: Jiao in his leisure often went to sit by the water, pacing and composing poetry, while official business was much neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao often spent his idle hours sitting by the water, wandering and composing verse while his official duties went largely undone.

sentences.zh: 令白府，以假尉代之，分其半奉。

translations.literal: The magistrate reported to the prefectural office, and an acting deputy was appointed in his stead, taking half his salary.
translations.idiomatic: The county magistrate reported to the prefecture; an acting deputy was installed to handle affairs, taking half of Jiao's stipend.

sentences.zh: 鄭余慶為東都留守，署水陸轉運判官。

translations.literal: Zheng Yuqing was eastern capital regent and appointed him Commissioner for Water and Land Transport.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuqing, as regent of the eastern capital, appointed him transport commissioner for water and land routes.

sentences.zh: 余慶鎮興元，奏為參謀。

translations.literal: When Yuqing governed Xingyuan, he memorialized to make [Jiao] staff adviser.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Yuqing took command at Xingyuan, he recommended Jiao as staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 張籍諡曰貞曜先生。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji gave him the posthumous title Master Zhenyao ("True Radiance").
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji honored him with the posthumous epithet Master True Radiance (Zhenyao).

sentences.zh: 郊為詩有理致，最為愈所稱，然思苦奇澀。

translations.literal: Jiao's poetry had reasoned structure and was most praised by Yu, yet his thought was laborious, strange, and austere.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao's poetry was rigorously structured and won Han Yu's highest praise, yet his verse was painstaking, strange, and austere.

sentences.zh: 李觀亦論其詩曰：「高處在古無上，平處下顧二謝」雲。

translations.literal: Li Guan also commented on his poetry, saying: "At its heights it stands above all antiquity; at its level passages it looks down upon the Two Xies," and so forth.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guan likewise wrote of his poetry: "At its heights it surpasses all antiquity; at its middling passages it still eclipses the Two Xies (Xie Lingyun and Xie Tiao)."

sentences.zh: 附 張籍

translations.literal: Appended: Zhang Ji
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Zhang Ji

sentences.zh: 張籍者，字文昌，和州烏江人。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji, styled Wenchang, was a native of Wujiang in Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji, courtesy name Wenchang, was from Wujiang in Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 第進士，為太常寺太祝。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as libationer in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed libationer in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 久次，遷秘書郎。

translations.literal: After long seniority, he was promoted to secretary of the imperial library.
translations.idiomatic: After long service in rank, he was promoted to secretary in the imperial archives.

sentences.zh: 愈薦為國子博士。

translations.literal: Han Yu recommended him for National University lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu recommended him for a lectureship at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 曆水部員外郎、主客郎中。

translations.literal: He successively served as vice director of the Waterways Bureau and director of the Bureau of Guests.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of vice-director in the Ministry of Works and director in the Ministry of Rites' Bureau of Foreign Guests.

sentences.zh: 當時有名士皆與游，而愈賢重之。

translations.literal: At the time all renowned scholars associated with him, while Yu esteemed him highly.
translations.idiomatic: All the celebrated men of the age counted him among their companions, and Han Yu held him in especial esteem.

sentences.zh: 籍性狷直，嘗責愈喜博褭及為駁雜之說，論議好勝人，其排釋老不能著書若孟軻、揚雄以垂世者。

translations.literal: Ji's nature was upright and blunt; he once reproached Yu for delighting in gambling and curios and for producing mixed, miscellaneous writings, debating to outdo others, and that his refutations of Buddhism and Taoism did not amount to books like Mencius and Yang Xiong to last through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: Blunt and uncompromising by nature, Zhang Ji once reproached Han Yu for his love of gambling and gewgaws, his miscellaneous essays, his habit of arguing to dominate others, and above all his failure to compose systematic refutations of Buddhism and Daoism on the scale of Mencius or Yang Xiong—works that might endure for ages.

sentences.zh: 愈最後答書曰：

translations.literal: Yu's final letter in reply said:
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu's final reply read:

sentences.zh: 吾子不以愈無似，意欲推之納諸聖賢之域，拂其邪心，增其所未高。

translations.literal: You do not regard Yu as unworthy; you intend to push him into the domain of sages and worthies, brush aside his perverse heart, and augment what heights he has not yet reached.
translations.idiomatic: You do not dismiss me as unworthy; you mean to lift me into the company of sages, to brush away my wayward impulses and raise me to heights I have not yet attained.

sentences.zh: 謂愈之質有可以至於道者，浚其源，道其所歸，溉其根，將食其實。

translations.literal: You say Yu's substance has that whereby one may reach the Way—dredging its source, showing where it leads, watering its roots, intending to eat its fruit.
translations.idiomatic: You believe my nature capable of reaching the Way—that you would dredge its source, point out its course, water its roots, and reap its fruit.

sentences.zh: 此盛德之所辭讓，況於愈者哉？

translations.literal: This is what great virtue courteously declines—how much more so for Yu?
translations.idiomatic: Such generosity is what the greatly virtuous modestly decline—how much more should I, Han Yu, decline it?

sentences.zh: 抑其中有宜復者，故不可遂已。

translations.literal: Yet among these points there are some that ought to be answered, and therefore one cannot simply stop.
translations.idiomatic: Yet some of your points deserve a reply, and I cannot simply let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 昔者聖人之作《春秋》也，既深其文辭矣，然猶不敢公傳道之，口授弟子，至於後世，其書出焉。

translations.literal: In former times, when the sage composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had already deepened its literary expression; yet he still dared not openly transmit the Way through it, but orally instructed his disciples; only in later generations did the book emerge.
translations.idiomatic: When the sage composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had already steeped its language in profundity, yet he still dared not openly transmit the Way through it—he taught his disciples by word of mouth, and only in later ages did the book appear.

sentences.zh: 其所以慮患之道，微也。

translations.literal: His manner of considering calamity was subtle indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the subtlety of his foresight against disaster.

sentences.zh: 今夫二氏之所宗而事之者，下及公卿輔相，吾豈敢昌言排之哉？

translations.literal: Now those whom the Two Schools revere and serve extend down to grandees and chief ministers—how dare I openly proclaim to refute them?
translations.idiomatic: Those whom Buddhism and Daoism command as adherents now include even grandees and chief ministers—how dare I proclaim open opposition?

sentences.zh: 擇其可語者誨之，猶時與吾悖，其聲嘵嘵。

translations.literal: Selecting those whom one may instruct, one teaches them; yet they still sometimes oppose me, their clamor noisy.
translations.idiomatic: Even when I select those fit to teach and instruct them, they still at times oppose me, their objections clamorous.

sentences.zh: 若遂成其書，則見而怒之者必多矣，必且以我為狂為惑。

translations.literal: If I were to complete such a book, those who saw it and grew angry would surely be many; they would surely take me for mad and deluded.
translations.idiomatic: Were I to complete such a systematic work, many who read it would be enraged; they would surely deem me mad or deluded.

sentences.zh: 其身之不能恤，書于何有？

translations.literal: If one cannot spare care for one's own person, what has one to do with books?
translations.idiomatic: If I cannot even protect my own person, what use is a book?

sentences.zh: 夫子，聖人也，而曰：「自吾得子路，而惡聲不入於耳。」

translations.literal: The Master was a sage, yet he said: "Since I obtained Zilu, no offensive sound has entered my ears."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius himself was a sage, yet he said, "Since I gained Zilu, no harsh word has reached my ears."

sentences.zh: 其餘輔而相者周天下，猶且絕糧于陳，畏于匡，毀于叔孫，奔走于齊、魯、宋、衛之郊。

translations.literal: Of the rest who assisted and supported him throughout the realm, still he suffered hunger in Chen, danger in Kuang, slander from Uncle Sun, and was driven in flight through the marches of Qi, Lu, Song, and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yet with helpers and ministers all across the realm, he still went hungry in Chen, was threatened at Kuang, was slandered by Uncle Sun, and was driven to wander the borders of Qi, Lu, Song, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 其道雖尊，其窮亦至矣。

translations.literal: Though his Way was honored, his extremity of destitution also reached its limit.
translations.idiomatic: Though his Way was supreme, his straits were the deepest imaginable.

sentences.zh: 賴其徒相與守之，卒有立於天下。

translations.literal: Relying on his disciples jointly to guard it, in the end it was established in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Only because his disciples together preserved it was it finally established in the world.

sentences.zh: 向使獨言之而獨書之，其存也可冀乎？

translations.literal: Had he spoken alone and written alone, could its preservation have been hoped for?
translations.idiomatic: Had he spoken and written entirely on his own, could it have survived at all?

sentences.zh: 今夫二氏行乎中土也，蓋六百年有餘矣。

translations.literal: Now the Two Schools operate in the Central Land—it has been roughly more than six hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism and Daoism have flourished in the Central Plains for well over six hundred years.

sentences.zh: 其植根固，其流波漫，非可以朝令而夕禁也。

translations.literal: Their roots planted are firm; their flowing waves spread wide—not something that can be forbidden at dawn and enforced by dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Their roots run deep, their currents spread wide—they cannot be banned by morning decree and extinguished by nightfall.

sentences.zh: 自文王沒，武王、周公、成、康相與守之，禮樂皆在，及乎夫子未久也，自夫子而至乎孟子未久也，自孟子而至乎揚雄亦未久也。

translations.literal: From the time King Wen died, King Wu, the Duke of Zhou, Cheng, and Kang jointly guarded it; rites and music were all present—and it had not been long until the Master; from the Master to Mencius had not been long; from Mencius to Yang Xiong had also not been long.
translations.idiomatic: From King Wen's death, King Wu, the Duke of Zhou, and the kings Cheng and Kang together preserved the Way—rites and music were intact—yet scarcely long had passed before Confucius; from Confucius to Mencius, scarcely long; from Mencius to Yang Xiong, scarcely long again.

sentences.zh: 然猶其勤若此，其困若此，而後能有所立，吾豈可易而為之哉？

translations.literal: Yet still their diligence was like this, their hardship like this, and only afterward could they establish something—how could I lightly undertake to do the same?
translations.idiomatic: Yet even with such diligence and such hardship they only then could establish something—how could I lightly attempt the same?

sentences.zh: 其為也易，則其傳也不遠，故餘所以不敢也。

translations.literal: If the doing is easy, then the transmission does not reach far—therefore this is why I dare not.
translations.idiomatic: What is done easily does not endure—that is why I dare not.

sentences.zh: 然觀古人，得其時，行其道，則無所為書。

translations.literal: Yet observing the ancients: when they obtained their time and practiced their Way, they had no need to write books.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the ancients: when the age was right and the Way could be practiced, they had no need to write.

sentences.zh: 為書者，皆所為不行乎今，而行乎後世者也。

translations.literal: Those who write books all do so because [the Way] cannot be practiced in the present, but can be practiced in later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Books are written only when the Way cannot be practiced in the present but may be practiced in ages to come.

sentences.zh: 今吾之得吾志、失吾志未可知，則俟五十、六十為之，未失也。

translations.literal: Now whether I attain or fail to attain my intent is not yet known; then to wait until fifty or sixty to do it would not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Whether I shall achieve my aims remains unknown; to wait until my fifties or sixties would not be too late.

sentences.zh: 天不欲使茲人有知乎，則吾之命不可期；

translations.literal: If Heaven does not wish this age's people to have such knowledge, then my allotted span cannot be foretold;
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven does not wish this generation to know the truth, then my span of life cannot be foreseen;

sentences.zh: 如使茲人有知乎，非我其誰哉！

translations.literal: if Heaven does wish this age's people to have such knowledge, who if not I?
translations.idiomatic: but if Heaven does wish this generation to know, who else if not I?

sentences.zh: 其行道，其為書，其化今，其傳後，必有在矣。

translations.literal: Whether in practicing the Way, in writing books, in transforming the present, or in transmitting to posterity—there is surely something [that will be accomplished].
translations.idiomatic: Whether in practicing the Way, writing books, transforming the present, or reaching posterity—something will surely come of it.

sentences.zh: 吾子其何遽戚戚於吾所為哉？

translations.literal: My lord, why so hastily fret and grieve over what I do?
translations.idiomatic: Why, my friend, do you fret so urgently over what I am doing?

sentences.zh: 前書謂吾與人論不能下氣，若好勝者。

translations.literal: Your earlier letter said that when I debate with others I cannot lower my qi, as if one who loves to win.
translations.idiomatic: Your earlier letter said that when I debate with others I cannot humble myself, as though I were someone who loves to win.

sentences.zh: 雖誠有之，抑非好己勝也，好己之道勝也。

translations.literal: Though that is truly so, yet it is not loving my own victory, but loving my own Way's victory.
translations.idiomatic: Though that is indeed true, it is not that I love my own victory, but that I love the victory of my Way.

sentences.zh: 非好己之道勝也，己之道乃夫子、孟軻、揚雄之道。

translations.literal: Nor is it loving my Way's victory—my Way is the Master's, Mencius's, and Yang Xiong's Way.
translations.idiomatic: Nor is it the victory of my Way that I love—my Way is the Way of the Master, Mencius, and Yang Xiong.

sentences.zh: 傳者若不勝，則無所為道，吾豈敢避是名哉！

translations.literal: If the transmitter does not prevail, then there is nothing to be done for the Way—how could I dare avoid this name!
translations.idiomatic: If the transmitter does not prevail, then nothing can be done for the Way—how could I dare shun that reputation!

sentences.zh: 夫子之言曰：「吾與回言，終日不違。」

translations.literal: The Master's words say: "When I speak with Hui, all day he does not contradict."
translations.idiomatic: The Master said: "When I talk with Hui, he does not contradict me all day."

sentences.zh: 如愚則其與眾人辯也有矣。

translations.literal: If he seemed stupid, then his debating with the multitude would exist.
translations.idiomatic: If he seemed stupid, then his debating with the multitude would make sense.

sentences.zh: 駁雜之譏，前書盡之，吾子其復之。

translations.literal: The criticism of mixed, miscellaneous [writings]—your earlier letter stated it fully; my lord, you may repeat it.
translations.idiomatic: The criticism of my miscellaneous writings—your earlier letter stated it fully; you may repeat it if you wish.

sentences.zh: 昔者夫子猶有所戲，《詩》不雲乎：「善戲謔兮，不為虐兮。」

translations.literal: In former times even the Master still had his play; does not the Book of Songs say: "Skillful is the jest and banter, yet it is not cruel"?"
translations.idiomatic: In former times even the Master still had his playful side. Does not the Book of Songs say: "Skillful is the jest and banter, yet it is not cruel"?

sentences.zh: 《記》曰：「張而不弛，文武不為也。」

translations.literal: The Record says: "To draw the bow without relaxing—this Wen and Wu would not do."
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says: "To draw the bow without ever relaxing—this is what King Wen and King Wu would not do."

sentences.zh: 惡害於道哉？

translations.literal: How could it harm the Way?"
translations.idiomatic: How could such things harm the Way?

sentences.zh: 吾子其未之思乎？

translations.literal: My lord, have you not yet thought of this?
translations.idiomatic: Have you, my friend, not yet considered this?

sentences.zh: 籍為詩，長於樂府，多警句。

translations.literal: Ji composed poetry, excelled in yuefu, and had many striking lines.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji wrote poetry, excelled in yuefu, and produced many striking lines.

sentences.zh: 仕終國子司業。

translations.literal: In office he ended as Vice Director of the National University Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his official career as Vice Director of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 附 皇甫湜

translations.literal: Appended: Huangfu Shi
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Huangfu Shi

sentences.zh: 皇甫湜，字持正，睦州新安人。

translations.literal: Huangfu Shi, style name Chizheng, was a man of Xin'an in Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Shi, whose style name was Chizheng, came from Xin'an in Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，為陸渾尉，仕至工部郎中，辨急使酒，數忤同省，求分司東都。

translations.literal: He was selected in the jinshi examination, served as magistrate of Luhun, and in office rose to director in the Ministry of Works; quick to argue and fond of wine, he often offended colleagues in the same bureau and sought a branch post at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, served as magistrate of Luhun, and rose to director in the Ministry of Works; quick-tempered and fond of wine, he often offended colleagues in the same ministry and sought a branch appointment at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 留守裴度辟為判官。

translations.literal: The defender-in-chief Pei Du engaged him as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital defender Pei Du took him on as an administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 度脩福先寺，將立碑，求文於白居易。

translations.literal: Du renovated Fuxian Temple and was about to erect a stele; he sought a text from Bai Juyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du was renovating Fuxian Temple and was about to erect a stele, he asked Bai Juyi for the inscription.

sentences.zh: 湜怒曰：「近舍湜而遠取居易，請從此辭。」

translations.literal: Shi angrily said: "You pass by Shi nearby yet go far to fetch Juyi—please accept my resignation from this."
translations.idiomatic: Shi said angrily: "You pass me by nearby and go far to fetch Juyi—please accept my resignation from this post."

sentences.zh: 度謝之。

translations.literal: Du apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du apologized to him.

sentences.zh: 湜即請鬥酒，飲酣，援筆立就。

translations.literal: Shi at once asked for a contest in wine; when drunk to satisfaction, he took up the brush and finished at once.
translations.idiomatic: Shi then asked for wine to drink in contest; when thoroughly drunk, he took up the brush and finished the text on the spot.

sentences.zh: 度贈以車馬繒彩甚厚，湜大怒曰：「自吾為《顧況集序》，未常許人。

translations.literal: Du presented him with carriages, horses, silks, and brocades in great quantity; Shi raged: "Since I wrote the Preface to the Gu Kuang Collection, I have never lightly promised anyone.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du gave him carriages, horses, silks, and brocades in great quantity; Shi flew into a rage: "Since I wrote the preface to Gu Kuang's collected works, I have never lightly promised anyone.

sentences.zh: 今碑字三千，字三縑，何遇我薄邪？」

translations.literal: Now the stele has three thousand characters—three bolts of silk per character—why do you treat me so thinly?"
translations.idiomatic: Now the stele has three thousand characters—three bolts of silk per character—why do you treat me so stingily?"

sentences.zh: 度笑曰：「不羈之才也。」

translations.literal: Du laughed and said: "An untrammeled talent indeed."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du laughed and said: "A truly untrammeled talent."

sentences.zh: 從而酬之。

translations.literal: He thereupon increased the payment.
translations.idiomatic: He then increased the payment.

sentences.zh: 湜嘗為蜂螫指，購小兒斂蜂，搗取其液。

translations.literal: Shi was once stung on the finger by a bee; he bought a small boy to collect bees and pound out their juice.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was once stung on the finger by a bee; he paid a boy to gather bees and pound out their venom.

sentences.zh: 一日命其子錄詩，一字誤，詬躍呼杖，杖未至，齧其臂血流。

translations.literal: One day he ordered his son to copy out poetry; one character was wrong, and he cursed and leaped, shouting for the cane; before the cane arrived he bit his own arm until blood flowed.
translations.idiomatic: One day he ordered his son to copy out a poem; on one wrong character he cursed and leaped about, shouting for the cane; before it arrived he bit his own arm until blood flowed.

sentences.zh: 附 盧仝

translations.literal: Appended: Lu Tong
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Lu Tong

sentences.zh: 盧仝居東都，愈為河南令，愛其詩，厚禮之。

translations.literal: Lu Tong dwelt in the Eastern Capital; Yu was magistrate of Henan, loved his poetry, and treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tong lived in the Eastern Capital; when Han Yu was magistrate of Henan he admired Tong's poetry and treated him with great generosity.

sentences.zh: 仝自號玉川子，嘗為《月蝕詩》以譏切元和逆黨，愈稱其工。

translations.literal: Tong styled himself Master Jade River; he once composed the "Ode on the Moon's Eclipse" to satirize the Yuanhe recalcitrants, and Yu praised its craft.
translations.idiomatic: Tong styled himself Master Jade River; he once wrote "Ode on the Moon's Eclipse" to satirize the Yuanhe faction, and Han Yu praised its workmanship.

sentences.zh: 時又有賈島、劉乂，皆韓門弟子。

translations.literal: At the time there were also Jia Dao and Liu Yi—all disciples of Han's school.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there were also Jia Dao and Liu Yi, both disciples of Han Yu's school.

sentences.zh: 附 賈島

translations.literal: Appended: Jia Dao
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Jia Dao

sentences.zh: 島，字浪仙，范陽人。

translations.literal: Dao, style name Langxian, was a man of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dao, courtesy name Langxian, was from Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 初為浮屠，名無本。

translations.literal: At first he was a Buddhist monk, named Wuben.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was a Buddhist monk under the name Wuben.

sentences.zh: 來東都，時洛陽令禁僧午後不得出，島為詩自傷。

translations.literal: He came to the Eastern Capital; at the time the Luoyang magistrate forbade monks to go out after noon, and Dao composed a poem lamenting himself.
translations.idiomatic: He came to the Eastern Capital; the Luoyang magistrate then forbade monks to go out after noon, and Dao wrote a poem lamenting his plight.

sentences.zh: 愈憐之，因教其為文，遂去浮屠，舉進士。

translations.literal: Yu pitied him and thereupon taught him to write prose; he then left the Buddhist clergy and entered the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu pitied him and taught him literary composition; Dao then left the clergy and entered the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 當其苦吟，雖逢值公卿貴人，皆不之覺也。

translations.literal: When he was bitterly composing poetry, even if he passed great ministers and nobles he did not notice them.
translations.idiomatic: When he was absorbed in composing poetry, even if he passed great ministers and nobles he took no notice of them.

sentences.zh: 一日見京兆尹，跨驢不避，謼詰之，久乃得釋。

translations.literal: One day he met the capital intendant, riding a donkey without yielding; he was rebuked and questioned, and only after a long while was he released.
translations.idiomatic: One day he encountered the capital intendant, riding a donkey without yielding; the intendant rebuked and questioned him, and only after a long while was he released.

sentences.zh: 累舉，不中第。

translations.literal: He repeatedly entered the examination but never placed.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly entered the examinations but never passed.

sentences.zh: 文宗時，坐飛謗，貶長江主簿。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wenzong, because of flying slander he was demoted to registrar of Changjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wenzong he was demoted to registrar of Changjiang on account of slander.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，以普州司倉參軍遷司戶，未受命卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huichang, from revenue adjutant of Puzhou he was transferred to registrar of the Household Bureau; before he received the appointment he died, age sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Huichang reign he was promoted from revenue adjutant in Puzhou to registrar of the Household Bureau; before he could take up the post he died, aged sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 附 劉乂

translations.literal: Appended: Liu Yi
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Liu Yi

sentences.zh: 劉乂者，亦一節士。

translations.literal: Liu Yi was also a man of resolute integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi was likewise a man of resolute integrity.

sentences.zh: 少放肆為俠行，因酒殺人亡命。

translations.literal: In youth he was unrestrained and pursued chivalric deeds; in a drunken fit he killed a man and fled for his life.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was unrestrained and pursued chivalric exploits; in a drunken fit he killed a man and fled as a fugitive.

sentences.zh: 會赦，出，更折節讀書，能為歌詩。

translations.literal: When an amnesty came he emerged, changed his conduct, and applied himself to reading; he could compose songs and poems.
translations.idiomatic: When an amnesty was proclaimed he came forth, reformed his conduct, and devoted himself to study; he could compose songs and poems.

sentences.zh: 然恃故時所負，不能俯仰貴人，常穿屐、破衣。

translations.literal: Yet relying on his former reputation he could not defer to the powerful; he often wore clogs and tattered clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet relying on his former reputation he could not bow and scrape before the powerful; he often wore clogs and tattered clothes.

sentences.zh: 聞愈接天下士，步歸之，作《冰柱》《雪車》二詩，出盧仝、孟郊右。

translations.literal: Hearing that Yu received men of talent from throughout the realm, he walked to join him and composed the two poems "Ice Columns" and "Snow Cart," ranking above Lu Tong and Meng Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Han Yu welcomed men of talent from throughout the realm, he walked to join him and composed the two poems "Ice Columns" and "Snow Cart," surpassing Lu Tong and Meng Jiao.

sentences.zh: 樊宗師見，為獨拜。

translations.literal: When Fan Zongshi saw them he bowed alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Zongshi saw them he bowed to him alone in homage.

sentences.zh: 能面道人短長，其服義則又彌縫若親屬然。

translations.literal: He could speak to people's faces of their faults and merits; where righteousness was concerned he would patch quarrels as if they were kin.
translations.idiomatic: He could speak to people's faces of their faults and merits; where righteousness was at stake he would mend quarrels as though they were kin.

sentences.zh: 後以爭語不能下賓客，因持愈金數斤去，曰：「此諛墓中人得耳，不若與劉君為壽。」

translations.literal: Later, because of a dispute in words he could not defer to guests; he took several jin of Yu's gold and left, saying: "This is what flattering grave-men obtain—better give it to Master Liu for his longevity."
translations.idiomatic: Later, because of a dispute in words he could not defer to guests; he took several jin of Han Yu's gold and left, saying: "This is what flatterers of the dead obtain—better give it to Master Liu for his longevity."

sentences.zh: 愈不能止，歸齊、魯，不知所終。

translations.literal: Yu could not stop him; he returned to Qi and Lu, and his end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu could not stop him; he returned to Qi and Lu, and his final whereabouts are unknown.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：唐興，承五代剖分，王政不綱，文弊質窮，崿俚混並。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: When Tang arose, inheriting the partitioned ruins of the Five Dynasties era, royal government lacked coherence, literary culture was exhausted in quality, and mountain-valley vulgarity mixed with the refined.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: When Tang arose, inheriting the partitioned realm left by five dynasties of division, royal government lacked coherence, literary culture was exhausted in substance, and rustic vulgarity mingled with the refined.

sentences.zh: 天下已定，治荒剔蠹，討究儒術，以興典憲，薰醲涵浸，殆百餘年，其後文章稍稍可述。

translations.literal: Once the realm was settled, they governed the wasteland and rooted out corruption, investigated Confucian learning to revive canonical institutions; steeped and permeated for nearly a hundred years, afterward writings gradually became worth recounting.
translations.idiomatic: Once the realm was settled, the court governed the wasteland and rooted out corruption, investigated Confucian learning to revive canonical institutions, and steeped the age for nearly a hundred years; only then did writings gradually become worth recounting.

sentences.zh: 至貞元、元和間，愈遂以《六經》之文為諸儒倡，障堤末流，反刓以樸，剗偽以真。

translations.literal: By the Zhenyuan and Yuanhe period, Yu thereupon took the text of the Six Classics to lead the Confucians, damming the terminal current, reversing carving toward simplicity, cutting falsehood for truth.
translations.idiomatic: By the Zhenyuan and Yuanhe reigns, Han Yu took the language of the Six Classics to lead the Confucians, damming the terminal current, reversing elaborate carving toward simplicity, and cutting away falsehood for truth.

sentences.zh: 然愈之才，自視司馬遷、揚雄，至班固以下不論也。

translations.literal: Yet Yu's talent—he regarded himself on a level with Sima Qian and Yang Xiong, and would not discuss [himself with] Ban Gu and those below.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in talent Han Yu ranked himself with Sima Qian and Yang Xiong, and would not even discuss Ban Gu and those below.

sentences.zh: 當其所得，粹然一出於正，刊落陳言，橫騖別驅，汪洋大肆，要之無牴牾聖人者。

translations.literal: When he hit his mark, [his writing] purely issued from the orthodox, pared away stale words, drove sideways in other tracks with vast expanse—in essentials nothing contradicted the sages.
translations.idiomatic: When he hit his mark, his writing issued purely from the orthodox, pared away stale formulas, and ranged abroad with vast force—yet in essentials it never contradicted the sages.

sentences.zh: 其道蓋自比孟軻，以荀況、揚雄為未淳，寧不信然？

translations.literal: His Way he largely compared himself to Mencius, considering Xun Kuang and Yang Xiong insufficiently pure—is this not believable?
translations.idiomatic: In the Way he largely compared himself to Mencius, deeming Xunzi and Yang Xiong insufficiently pure—is this not credible?

sentences.zh: 至進諫陳謀，排難恤孤，矯拂媮末，皇皇于仁義，可謂篤道君子矣。

translations.literal: As for advancing remonstrance and offering stratagems, resolving difficulties and succoring the orphaned, correcting frivolous ends—earnest in humanity and righteousness—he may be called a devoted follower of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: In advancing remonstrance and offering counsel, resolving difficulties and succoring the orphaned, and correcting frivolous ends, he was earnest in humanity and righteousness—he may truly be called a devoted follower of the Way.

sentences.zh: 自晉汔隋，老佛顯行，聖道不斷如帶。

translations.literal: From Jin through Sui, Laozi and Buddha were conspicuous, and the sage's Way hung by a thread.
translations.idiomatic: From Jin through Sui, Laozi and the Buddha were conspicuous, and the sage's Way hung by a thread.

sentences.zh: 諸儒倚天下正議，助為怪神。

translations.literal: The Confucians leaned on the realm's orthodox judgment and helped fashion weird spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The Confucians leaned on the realm's orthodox judgment yet helped fashion strange spirits.

sentences.zh: 愈獨喟然引聖，爭四海之惑，雖蒙訕笑，跲而復奮，始若未之信，卒大顯于時。

translations.literal: Only Yu sighed and summoned the sage, contending with the doubts of all within the seas; though he suffered mockery, stumbled, and rose again, at first as if not believed, he finally shone greatly in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu alone sighed and summoned the sage, contending with the doubts of all under Heaven; though mocked, he stumbled yet rose again, at first scarcely believed, yet finally shone greatly in his own time.

sentences.zh: 昔孟軻拒楊、墨，去孔子才二百年。

translations.literal: Formerly Mencius resisted Yang Zhu and Mozi, only two hundred years from Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Mencius resisted Yang Zhu and Mozi, only two hundred years after Confucius.

sentences.zh: 愈排二家，乃去千餘歲，撥衰反正，功與齊而力倍之，所以過況、雄為不少矣。

translations.literal: Yu repelled the two schools nearly a thousand years later, pulling decay back to the orthodox—his achievement matched [Mencius] and his power doubled it; thus he surpassed Xun and Yang by no small measure.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu repelled the two schools nearly a thousand years later, pulling decay back to the orthodox; his achievement matched Mencius and his force doubled it—thus he surpassed Xunzi and Yang Xiong by no small measure.

sentences.zh: 自愈沒，其言大行，學者仰之如泰山、北斗雲。

translations.literal: From Yu's death his words ran widely; scholars looked up to him as to Mount Tai and the Northern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: From Han Yu's death his words spread widely; scholars looked up to him as to Mount Tai and the Northern Dipper.
